title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Length-aware candidate block selection in the decode indexer
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1's decode indexer writes its logits into a `[rows, max_model_len]` buffer, a width that must stay static for CUDA graphs (1M with the default `max_model_len`). Each row only holds its own context, but `select_candidate_blocks` scored every block of the full width and then ran `torch.topk(2048)` over all of them. At 1M that costs about 850 us per decode step, whatever the actual context length. This PR makes candidate selection length-aware.

- **Score only valid blocks.** `_block_scores_kernel` now runs a fixed `(rows, 32)` grid that walks each row's tiles only up to the row's end, and it writes each row's valid block count.
- **DeepSelect instead of `torch.topk`.** On the DeepSelect path, the block count is passed as DeepSelect's per-row `end`. Short rows are padded with -1. Candidate order does not matter, because the sparse expansion sorts. The full-width `torch.topk` path stays as the fallback for no DeepSelect, non-contiguous output, `topk > 4096` and narrow logits, and its behaviour is unchanged.
- **NaN rows.** DeepSelect leaves NaN rows only partly written, which can happen during warmup or capture on an uninitialized KV cache. On the DeepSelect path, NaN blocks are pinned like the newest block, as `torch.topk` ranks NaN first. NaN rows therefore still get complete, in-range candidates.
- **bf16 decode logits.** The decode indexer now asks DeepGEMM for bf16 logits when the top-k backend is `deep_select` and DCP is off. This halves the bytes that the top-k and candidate passes read. The logits kernel still accumulates in fp32 and only rounds the output, which is byte-identical to `bf16(fp32 logits)`. The other top-k backends and the DCP merge still get fp32.
- **Footprint.** `candidate_blocks.py`, the decode call in `sparse_attn_indexer.py`, and a `logits_dtype` passthrough on `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` (default fp32). The DeepSelect availability check reuses `has_deep_select()`.

## Kernel microbenchmark

`select_candidate_blocks` alone, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode shapes: 384 rows (64 requests x 6 tokens), logits width 1,048,576 (default `max_model_len`, ratio-1 candidate-source layer), 2048 candidate blocks of 8. 1 x GB300, FlashInfer CUPTI timing with CUDA graph replay and cold L2, median. Logits are continuous random values; random FP4 inputs give heavily tied logits, which is pathological for radix selection and does not match the model.

| context (tokens) | main, fp32 logits (us) | this PR, fp32 logits (us) | this PR, bf16 logits (us) | speedup (bf16 vs main) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 131,072 | 847.8 | 77.0 | 42.9 | 19.8x |
| 176,000 | 861.2 | 116.8 | 62.2 | 13.8x |
| 400,000 | 884.0 | 205.9 | 119.9 | 7.4x |
| 1,048,576 | 939.0 | 408.2 | 254.9 | 3.7x |

main's cost is flat because it always scores and sorts the full width. This PR scales with the context and is still faster at the full 1M.

The dense indexer top-k reads the same logits, so the bf16 switch also speeds it up. DeepSelect top-512 at 131K context, ratio-2 layer (65K keys) / ratio-1 layer (131K keys): fp32 42.2 / 62.7 us, bf16 28.8 / 45.4 us. The logits kernel itself takes the same time with fp32 and bf16 output (93.0 vs 94.2 us, 180.6 vs 181.5 us).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py -q -k "candidate or sparse_topk_remap"
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py
```

Also checked locally, without adding tests:
- Against the previous implementation, on 384-row decode inputs (1M width, random ends, `row_repeat=6`, rows shorter than 2048 blocks, empty rows, ends past the width), prefill rows with starts, and the fallback path: the selected candidate sets are identical. The only exception is an exact score tie at the 2048th block, where either choice is valid.
- The fallback path forced on is identical to the previous implementation (fp32). With bf16 logits, the DeepSelect path and the fallback select the same blocks, compared by score so ties do not count.
- NaN rows (fully NaN, and partly NaN) on the DeepSelect path: every id is in range and unique, nothing stale is left, and the NaN blocks are selected.
- bf16 paged MQA logits are byte-identical to the fp32 output rounded to bf16.

## Test Result

On 1 x GB300: 6 passed (the four `test_candidate_kernels_preserve_packed_bounds_and_padding` cases, including `out[:, ::2]` at 32768 columns, `test_select_candidate_blocks_tolerates_empty_rows`, and `test_sparse_topk_remap_bounds_nan_rows`). Pre-commit (ruff, format, typos, mypy) passes.

## E2E decode (DEP4)

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (DP4 x TP1 + EP) on one GB300 node. `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41` with the MXFP4 indexer cache and sparse indexer logits, DeepGEMM mega MoE, `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend deep_select`, DSpark (5 tokens, synthetic acceptance), `max_num_seqs=64`, default `max_model_len` (1M), `DecodeBenchConnector`. 256 random-token requests with 125,000 input and 8,000 output tokens, all admitted at once. The nsys window opens about 40 s in, at a context of about 131K. GPU time is per decode step and GPU, averaged over all GPU-steps in the window. The E2E runs used a DSv4.1 development tree whose `candidate_blocks.py` and `sparse_attn_indexer.py` are identical to main's, with and without this patch; the unit tests ran on this branch.

| | base | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| indexer + candidate selection (us/step) | 1698 | 886 |
| `_block_scores_kernel` (us/step) | 208 | 26 |
| `torch.topk` kernels (`computeBlockDigitCounts`, `gatherTopK`, sort, ...) (us/step) | 619 | 0 |
| target forward GPU busy (ms/step) | 24.11 | 23.36 |
| median ITL (ms) | 26.52 | 25.65 |

A rerun with the final code gives the same 886 us.

## Accuracy

GSM8K with lm-eval 0.4.13 on this PR: 1319 problems, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, 1024-token cap, concurrency 32, one DEP4 `vllm serve` (MegaAttn, MXFP4 indexer cache with sparse logits, DeepGEMM mega MoE, `deep_select` top-k, so the decode indexer runs with bf16 logits and the new selection path). DSpark used 5 speculative tokens with standard rejection sampling and adaptive verification off. Acceptance comes from the `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters over the eval.

| | strict match | flexible extract | acceptance length, incl. bonus | per-position acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| this PR | **92.57%** | 92.49% (±0.7) | **3.423** | 0.790 / 0.646 / 0.452 / 0.329 / 0.205 |
| #59923 (DSpark, adaptive verification on) | 92.57% | | 3.398 | 0.795 / 0.644 / 0.446 / 0.319 / 0.194 |
| #59511 base (DSpark, adaptive verification on) | 92.57% | | 3.365 | 0.792 / 0.641 / 0.441 / 0.310 / 0.181 |

GSM8K contexts are short (under 16K tokens), so the candidate-source layer keeps every valid block either way. Here the bf16 logits mainly feed the dense top-512. No accuracy or acceptance change is claimed.

<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve <model> --served-model-name DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --language-model-only \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --sparse-indexer-topk-backend deep_select --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"embedding_across_dp":true,"dp_shared_memory":true,"use_thp":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"standard","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[6,12,...,384],"max_cudagraph_capture_size":384}'

lm-eval run --model local-completions \
  --model_args "model=DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8010/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None" \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs "max_gen_toks=1024,temperature=0"
```

</details>

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `select_candidate_blocks`, `candidate_blocks`, `candidate blocks DeepSelect`, `indexer candidate topk` and `DSv4.1 indexer bf16 logits`. #59668 fuses the ROCm candidate mask (`rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`) and does not touch candidate selection.

title: [Perf] Warm up DeepGEMM MegaMoE kernels before serving
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution -->
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The DeepGEMM warmup covers `fp8_gemm_nt` and the grouped MoE GEMM. It does not cover `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` or the `bf16_mega_gate` that routes into it. With `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi K3 therefore JIT-compile these kernels on the first request at each new prefill size. This PR adds them to `deep_gemm_warmup.py`, following the structure of the two existing DeepGEMM warmups there.

## Claims

- No serving-time compiles of the MegaMoE kernels: `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, `bf16_mega_gate` and the Triton input-staging kernel. Before: 60 DeepGEMM compiles in one DeepSeek-V4 benchmark run. For Kimi K3, the 2 SiTU `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` compiles during serving that cost 2.6-2.9 s of TTFT each go to 0, at about +10 s of startup.
- MTP speculative decoding needs nothing extra. The DeepSeek-V4 MTP drafter's MegaMoE layer uses the same kernels as the target's, and there were 0 DeepGEMM compiles during serving with MTP on.
- DeepSeek-V4: the first request at a new prefill size no longer stalls for 3.5 to 6 s. It now takes about the same time as a repeat. The exception is a one-time 60-85 ms communication-buffer setup on the server's first large prefill, which is not a compile (see Details).
- Cost: for DeepSeek-V4, the first startup on a cold DeepGEMM cache takes about 4 to 5 min longer (+247 to +299 s on fully empty caches). A warm restart takes the same time as before. For Kimi K3, it is about +10 s.

## Validation

**Setup (DeepSeek-V4).** DeepSeek-V4-Flash on 2x B300, TP2 + EP2, `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, `max_num_batched_tokens` 16384, `--max-model-len 16384`, prefix caching off, Model Runner V2. vLLM precompiled wheel `3ca00a82` (cu130) with its bundled DeepGEMM.

Each run used a fresh `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR` seeded with every non-mega DeepGEMM kernel, so only the mega kernels start cold.

**Workload.** One request at a time: token-ID prompts to `/v1/completions`, `max_tokens` 4, streamed time to first token (TTFT).
1. Six fixed lengths (100 to 8000 tokens). Each gets a first request, then 3 repeats with new random tokens.
2. 40 seeded random lengths from 51 to 15504 tokens. The warmup did not pick these.
3. 32 concurrent requests.

**JIT compiles during serving.** Counted as new entries in the DeepGEMM cache dir between "Application startup complete" and the end of the workload, across all kernel families. Triton, CuTeDSL and TileLang compiles were counted with `--jit-monitor-verbose`.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `sm100_bf16_mega_gate` | 58 | 0 |
| `sm100_fp8_fp4_mega_moe` | 2 | 0 |
| other DeepGEMM families | 0 | 0 |
| Triton `_prepare_megamoe_inputs_kernel` | ≥1 (see note) | 0 |

On main, the Triton row comes from the default (non-verbose) JIT monitor, which logs only the first compile per kernel, so the true count is unknown. The previous revision of this PR, which warmed without a padding mask, compiled 3 variants for just three prompt lengths in a verbose run.

A separate single-GPU check called both kernels for every per-rank token count from 1 to 8192 after the warmup's representative sizes. It produced 0 new cache entries. An independent rerun of the patched server, with 20 prompt lengths, 16 of them chosen to give unaligned per-rank chunks, saw 0 JIT events.

**TTFT, first request vs median of 3 repeats (ms):**

| prompt tokens | main, first | main, repeat | this PR, first | this PR, repeat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000 | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 |
| 2000 | 3503 | 106 | 112 | 103 |
| 4000 | 5913 | 119 | 178 | 117 |
| 8000 | 3489 | 136 | 141 | 136 |

- 40 random lengths: 24 of the 40 requests on main took 3.5 to 6.0 s. The slowest on this PR took 0.27 s. Total TTFT went from 90.1 s to 6.1 s.
- 32 concurrent requests: worst TTFT went from 8.33 s to 1.47 s.

**Startup, `init engine` (profile, KV cache, warmup, graph capture):**

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| cold mega-kernel cache (all other kernels cached) | 141 s | 428 s |
| fully empty caches, no MTP (separate tester run) | 444 s | 691 s (+247 s) |
| fully empty caches, with MTP (separate tester run) | 406 s | 705 s (+299 s) |
| warm restart, same cache dir | 63 s | 63 s |

KV cache sizing is unchanged: 163.13 GiB and 465,145 tokens in both.

**MTP (DeepSeek-V4, `--speculative_config.method=mtp --speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens=2`, same setup and workload):**

| MegaMoE compiles during serving | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| seeded cache (mega kernels cold), 1 run | not run | 0 |
| fully empty caches, 1 run (separate tester) | 2 `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, 10 `bf16_mega_gate`, 6 Triton staging | 0 |

On this PR's commit with MTP: the server was healthy, GSM8K (200 questions, 5-shot) scored 0.970, and mean MTP acceptance length was 2.62 on GSM8K. On the random-token benchmark, acceptance was 1.61, against 1.55 on the previous revision. DeepGEMM compiles during serving: 0.

The drafter needs no extra warmup. Its MegaMoE layer reuses the target's kernels, and the tester's tracer saw no DeepGEMM compile in the drafter during serving on either build.

**Kimi K3 (`mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75`, a pruned checkpoint):** 4x B300, TP4 + EP4 with sequence parallelism, `max_num_batched_tokens` 8192 (2048 per rank), fp8 KV, no prefix caching, no spec decode.
- Each run started with empty DeepGEMM, Triton, Inductor and vLLM caches. One run per build.
- Workload: one 3000-token request, a second 3000-token request with new tokens, then 137, 1500, 5000 and 8000 tokens.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| DeepGEMM compiles during serving | 2 (`fp8_fp4_mega_moe` SiTU, `block_m` 128 and 192) | 0 |
| Triton `_prepare_megamoe_inputs_kernel` compiled during serving | yes (ranks 1-3, first request) | no |
| TTFT at 1500 / 5000 tokens | 2734 / 3139 ms | 153 / 244 ms |
| `init engine` | 46 s* | 56-57 s |

\*The main run had a warm FlashInfer JIT cache from an earlier run. The PR runs had one too, so the +10 s compares like with like.

On both builds, two non-MegaMoE kernels still compile during serving: the Inductor kernel `triton_poi_fused_mul_sigmoid_0`, on the first prefill above the capture sizes, and the KDA gated RMSNorm Triton kernel `layer_norm_gated_fwd_kernel`. They are outside this PR.

**Fully cold cache.** With every DeepGEMM and Triton cache empty (not just the mega kernels), three other DeepGEMM kernel families still compile on first use with this PR. They are outside MegaMoE and left for follow-ups:
- `fp8_einsum` in `o_proj` (`sm100_fp8_gemm_1d1d`): 2 kernels.
- `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm`: 8 kernels without MTP, 6 with MTP.
- The sparse indexer's `sm100_mqa_logits`: 1 kernel.

With MTP, the spec-decode rejection-sampler Triton kernels also compile on first use on both builds. That is unrelated to this PR.

**Tests.** `tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py` adds two CPU tests:
- The layer predicate is False for other models, and neither model module is imported. It is True only for DeepSeek-V4 and Kimi K3 MegaMoE layers.
- The warmup sizes for each `bf16_mega_gate` config are above the gate's token threshold, so the forward reaches the kernel.

All 8 tests pass.

**CI gap.** This path needs SM100 GPUs, DeepSeek-V4 or Kimi K3 with the native MegaMoE backend, and expert parallelism. CI has no such setup, so the validation above was run by hand.

<details>
<summary>Repro commands</summary>

```bash
# server (baseline: same command on main)
export VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=1 DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR=<fresh dir>
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=mxfp4 \
  --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --no-enable-prefix-caching --jit-monitor-verbose --port 8234

# client: fixed lengths x (1 first + 3 repeats), 40 random lengths, 32-request burst;
# records TTFT and the new DeepGEMM cache entries per request
SWEEP=40 python bench.py 8234 $DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR results.json
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>bench.py</summary>

```python
"""First-hit benchmark. Phase 1 (fixed): for each prompt length, one request
at a time: a first hit, then REPEATS more with fresh random tokens. Phase 2
(sweep, optional): random lengths the warmup did not pick, then a concurrent
burst (mixed prefill + decode). Records TTFT and every DeepGEMM JIT cache
entry created during serving, per kernel family."""
import collections, concurrent.futures as cf, json, os, random, re, sys, time
import requests

port, dgdir, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3]
LENGTHS = [int(x) for x in os.environ.get("LENGTHS", "100,400,1000,2000,4000,8000").split(",")]
REPEATS = int(os.environ.get("REPEATS", "3"))
SWEEP = int(os.environ.get("SWEEP", "0"))
URL = f"http://localhost:{port}/v1/completions"
MODEL = "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash"
cache = os.path.join(dgdir, "cache")

def entries():
    return set(os.listdir(cache))

def family(e):
    m = re.match(r"(?:kernel\.)?(.+?)\.[0-9a-f]{32}$", e)
    return m.group(1) if m else e

def fam_count(es):
    return dict(collections.Counter(family(e) for e in es))

def ttft(prompt_ids, max_tokens=4):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    r = requests.post(URL, json=dict(model=MODEL, prompt=prompt_ids, max_tokens=max_tokens,
                                     temperature=0, stream=True, ignore_eos=True),
                      stream=True, timeout=3600)
    first = None
    for line in r.iter_lines():
        if line and line.startswith(b"data: ") and line != b"data: [DONE]" and first is None:
            first = time.perf_counter() - t0
    return first, time.perf_counter() - t0

rng = random.Random(0)
def prompt(L):
    return [rng.randrange(1000, 100000) for _ in range(L)]

start = entries()
print(f"entries at ready: {len(start)} {fam_count(start)}", flush=True)
rows = []
ttft(prompt(8))  # HTTP/tokenizer warm; 4 per-rank tokens -> no mega gate
for L in LENGTHS:
    for i in range(1 + REPEATS):
        before = entries()
        t, e2e = ttft(prompt(L))
        new = entries() - before
        rows.append(dict(phase="fixed", prompt_len=L, rep="first" if i == 0 else f"repeat{i}",
                         ttft_s=t, e2e_s=e2e, new=fam_count(new)))
        print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
after_fixed = entries()
sweep_lengths = []
if SWEEP:
    srng = random.Random(1)
    sweep_lengths = sorted(srng.randrange(17, 16380) for _ in range(SWEEP))
    for L in sweep_lengths:
        before = entries()
        t, e2e = ttft(prompt(L))
        rows.append(dict(phase="sweep", prompt_len=L, rep="first", ttft_s=t, e2e_s=e2e,
                         new=fam_count(entries() - before)))
        print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
    # concurrent burst: 32 requests, mixed lengths, 64 output tokens -> prefill + decode mix
    burst = [prompt(srng.randrange(17, 6000)) for _ in range(32)]
    before = entries(); t0 = time.perf_counter()
    with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(32) as ex:
        res = list(ex.map(lambda p: ttft(p, 64), burst))
    rows.append(dict(phase="burst", prompt_len=-1, rep="32 concurrent", ttft_s=max(r[0] for r in res),
                     e2e_s=time.perf_counter() - t0, new=fam_count(entries() - before)))
    print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True)
end = entries()
summary = dict(rows=rows, entries_at_ready=fam_count(start), new_during_fixed=fam_count(after_fixed - start),
               new_during_serving=fam_count(end - start), new_entries=sorted(end - start),
               sweep_lengths=sweep_lengths)
json.dump(summary, open(out, "w"), indent=1)
print("new during serving:", summary["new_during_serving"])
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** Both kernels choose a JIT config from the per-rank token count:
- `bf16_mega_gate`: block tokens, MMA CTAs, split-K, expert groups and stages (`heuristics/mega_gate.hpp`). That is 87 configs for per-rank sizes 17 to 8192.
- `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`: `block_m` in {16, 32, 64, 128, 192, 240}.

Startup only compiles the sizes that the profile run and CUDA graph capture hit, here 512 or fewer tokens per rank. Every other prefill size compiles on first use, about 1.7 s per kernel. DeepSeek-V4 needs two gate kernels per size, because hash-routed and bias-routed layers pass different optional inputs.

**Design.** The warmup lives in `deep_gemm_warmup.py`, with the same parts as the existing DeepGEMM warmups:
- A layer predicate that matches DeepSeek-V4's `DeepseekV4MoE` and Kimi K3's `KimiMoE` when they use the native MegaMoE backend.
- A cache constant.
- `_get_fp8_fp4_mega_moe_m_values`: for every per-rank size, it asks DeepGEMM for the `block_m` and, for DeepSeek-V4, the gate config. It keeps the largest size of each distinct config (95 sizes for DeepSeek-V4 here), because DeepSeek-V4 only calls `bf16_mega_gate` above a small token threshold and a config's largest size is always above it. The configs come from DeepGEMM's own getters, so the dedup is exact and `VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=full` would add nothing.
  - Kimi K3 routes with its `GateLinear`, which the bf16x3 router warmup already covers, so for Kimi only `block_m` matters.
  - Kimi's experts call the SiTU variant of `fp8_fp4_mega_moe`, which picks `block_m` with the same heuristic.
- A private worker and a public loop, an `elif` branch in `_count_warmup_iterations`, and calls in `deep_gemm_warmup`.

The worker runs the whole MoE layer at each size, not the raw kernels:
- The gate gets the same optional inputs it gets in serving.
- Every EP rank runs the same sizes in the same order, which the collective MegaMoE kernel needs.
- It runs under a minimal forward context with a padding mask, because the layer reads `is_padding` from the forward context. This makes the Triton input-staging kernel compile the variants serving uses.
- Under sequence parallelism with `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING` on (the default), ranks above 0 get mask slices at any alignment, so each size runs once with an aligned slice and once with an unaligned one.

The predicate looks the model modules up in `sys.modules`, as other model-specific warmups in this package do (`kimi_k3_triton_warmup.py`, `qwen4_exp_qsa_warmup.py`), so other models import neither model. The cache key reads two DeepSeek-V4-only attributes (`tid2eid`, `image_sentinel_lo`) with `getattr`, because they do not exist on Kimi K3. The two config getters are reached through `_import_deep_gemm`, as in the model code.

`models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py` gains one line, which stores `use_sequence_parallel` on `KimiMoE` as `DeepseekV4MoE` already does. The warmup needs it to compute the per-rank token count.

<details>
<summary>Startup trade-off: where the cold warmup time goes</summary>

- About 84% of the cold warmup is serial `nvcc` time for 136 gate kernels (1.7 s each).
- About 14% is about 24 Triton staging variants.
- About 3% is 3 MegaMoE kernels.
- The layer forwards and the size search take under 1 s.

Compiling in parallel threads crashed inside DeepGEMM's JIT, which has no locking and no compile-only API. Parallel compilation would need DeepGEMM changes. vLLM keeps the DeepGEMM cache in `~/.cache/vllm/deep_gemm`, so the cold cost is paid once per machine and DeepGEMM version.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Remaining one-time first-request cost</summary>

The first eager prefill whose reduce-scatter falls in the MNNVL multimem size range sets up a symmetric-memory buffer (`_init_mnnvl_multimem_reduce_scatter_buffer`). This adds 60-85 ms to that one request (+61, +66 and +83 ms in three runs). CUDA graph capture skips this setup. It is paid once per server and is not a compile. A torch profile and a request-order test confirm both points.
</details>

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Seed the -1 sentinel in the prefill sparse index workspace
body:
## Overview

Port #55299 to the DeepSeek-V4.1 copy of `combine_topk_swa_indices`: seed a caller-provided `out=` buffer with the `-1` sentinel before the kernel writes each row's valid prefix. Without it, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill through FlashMLA mega attention reads stale indices and produces NaN; in our deployment this surfaced as an intermittent illegal memory access.

## Claims

- Fixes NaN attention outputs in DSv4.1 FlashMLA mega-attention prefill for rows whose combined index list is shorter than the padded width: the first 127 tokens of a fresh prompt, the rows right after an SWA bounded-replay start, and compressed-layer rows that have fewer than `index_topk` candidates.
- The NaN spreads through the KV cache into later tokens and layers, including the indexer, where `top_k_per_row_prefill` turns NaN logits into out-of-range indices (#49896). In our downstream build, which also runs the decoder replay tail as one FULL CUDA graph (not in `main`), those indices reached `_compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel` and crashed with an illegal memory access; this fix removes that crash there.
- One line, identical to the #55299 fix in `deepseek_v4`.

## Validation

GB200, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, FlashMLA mega attention, MXFP4 indexer cache, breakable CUDA graphs (`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`). The kernel repro was run twice: with our vLLM 0.30-based build, and with `main`'s `cache_utils.py` (e161a0798c) loaded over it, with identical results. `main`'s combine kernel additionally masks invalid top-k candidates, but like ours it never writes `[combined_len, width)`. The E2E run used the downstream build.

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Kernel repro (below), `main`'s `combine_topk_swa_indices` + `fused_norm_rope_attn_rope_cast_fwd`, `out=` pre-filled with in-range indices of NaN KV rows; NaN output rows | 96/300 (SWA-only, width 128), 768/1200 (ratio 2, width 640), 352/700 (ratio 1, width 640) | 0 / 0 / 0, no stale tail entry |
| Same kernel, tail entries set to `-1`, out of range, or pointing at finite rows | output bit-identical in all three | n/a |
| E2E, downstream prefill serving stack, DP4/EP4 on 4x GB200; per DP rank, a fresh 600-1300-token prompt plus a prefix hit (16K-60K prefix) within 40 ms at 2 pairs/s, plus long fresh prompts | illegal memory access 2 s into the workload | 900 s, 13,801 requests; 0 illegal memory access, 0 CUDA errors |

No test is added, as in #55299: CI has no GB200 runner exercising DSv4.1 FlashMLA mega attention, so the validation above was done outside CI.

In the downstream build, a GPU core dump of the crash places it in `_compute_global_topk_indices_and_lens_kernel` (block-table load) in the replay-tail FULL graph, and per-row NaN probes show the first real-row NaN at the layer-1 input (layer 0 is pure SWA). No accuracy eval was run: rows that never hit a stale tail are unchanged (second row of the table), and the change only restores the sentinel the kernel contract already assumes.

<details>
<summary>Kernel repro</summary>

```python
import torch

import vllm.v1.attention.ops.flashmla  # noqa: F401  registers _flashmla_C
from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.ops import combine_topk_swa_indices
from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.ops.fused_layout import WV_GROUP_SIZE
from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.flash_mla_mega_attn import (
    _HEAD_DIM_V, _ROPE_ARGS, _SF_ARGS, alloc_mega_attn_output,
)

H, D, W, TOPK = 64, 512, 128, 512
dev = "cuda"
g = torch.Generator(device=dev).manual_seed(0)


def case(n, top_k, ratio, comp_rows):
    m = comp_rows + n + 2048  # kv rows: compressed | swa | never written
    kv = (torch.randn(m, 1, D, device=dev, generator=g) * 0.5).bfloat16()
    kv[comp_rows + n :] = float("nan")
    q = (torch.randn(n, H, D, device=dev, generator=g) * 0.5).bfloat16()
    pos = torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    col = torch.arange(TOPK, device=dev)[None, :]
    topk = torch.where(col < ((pos + 1) // max(ratio, 1))[:, None], col, -1).int()
    width = (top_k + W + 127) // 128 * 128
    # A workspace slice holding stale in-range indices from an earlier call.
    idx_ws = (comp_rows + n + torch.arange(width, device=dev)).repeat(n, 1).int()
    lens_ws = torch.empty(n, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    qsl = torch.tensor([0, n], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    seq = torch.tensor([n], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    idx, lens = combine_topk_swa_indices(
        topk, qsl, seq, seq, W, ratio, top_k, m, comp_rows, out=(idx_ws, lens_ws)
    )
    out = alloc_mega_attn_output(n, H // WV_GROUP_SIZE, torch.device(dev))
    torch.ops._flashmla_C.fused_norm_rope_attn_rope_cast_fwd(
        q, kv, idx.unsqueeze(1), D**-0.5, _HEAD_DIM_V, torch.zeros(H, device=dev),
        lens, False, 0.0, pos, *_ROPE_ARGS,
        torch.randn(65536, 64, device=dev, generator=g), H // WV_GROUP_SIZE,
        *_SF_ARGS, out.data, out.scale,
    )
    nan = ((out.data.view(torch.uint8) & 0x7F) == 0x7F).flatten(1).any(1)
    print(f"ratio={ratio} width={width} nan_rows={int(nan.sum())}/{n}")


case(300, 0, 0, 0)      # SWA-only layer
case(1200, TOPK, 2, 1024)
case(700, TOPK, 1, 1024)
```

</details>

## Details

`combine_topk_swa_indices` writes `[0, combined_len)` of each row and relies on the rest being `-1`, which `topk_length` pairs with. The `out=None` branch gets that from `torch.full(-1)`; the `out=` branch does not seed it. Both NVIDIA callers pass a workspace slice (`flash_mla_mega_attn.py` prefill, `flashmla.py`), so the tail holds whatever an earlier user of the arena left there.

The FlashMLA prefill kernel processes the index list in whole `B_TOPK` tiles (the reason for the 128 alignment) and still loads the KV rows of a tile's entries past `topk_length`, masking them to p = 0. A stale in-range index that lands on a `kv_ws` row this call did not write brings in arbitrary bytes, and 0 * NaN = NaN, so the masked entry still poisons the output row. Rows with a short window are the ones with a tail: at layer 0 (width 128) a fresh prompt's positions 0-126; in compressed layers (width 640) every row with fewer than 512 top-k candidates or a window shorter than 128 (for example right after an SWA bounded-replay start).

#55299 fixed exactly this in `deepseek_v4/common/ops/cache_utils.py`. The `deepseek_v41` package was added afterwards by #56228 from an older copy of that file: its `combine_topk_swa_indices` matched the pre-#55299 V4 version line for line when it was added, and has never had the line.

Cost: one memset of `rows x width` int32 per call (about 20 MiB for an 8K-token chunk at width 640). Writing the tail inside the Triton kernel would avoid it, but would duplicate the padded-width formula in the kernel and diverge from the V4 fix; this keeps the fix the same in both packages.

Not a duplicate: open PRs touching `combine_topk_swa_indices` are ROCm-only (#60091, #56638). #59131 reworks the same prefill path but still passes the workspace as `out=`, so it depends on this fix as well.

title: [Bugfix][Kernel] persistent_topk: don't select float4 tail lanes past the row length
body:
## Overview

FIX #62466

`histogram_2048_topk` in `csrc/persistent_topk.cuh` can return indices `>= seq_len`. This happens when the row length is not a multiple of 4 and the top-k threshold lands in the fp16 `-inf` bin. This PR skips lanes past `seq_len` in the collection loop and adds a regression test.

## Claims

- `persistent_topk` no longer returns indices past the row length on the `histogram_2048_topk` path (k < length <= 8192, at most 32 rows).
- The out-of-bounds reads of `logits` in the refinement pass are gone.
- Rows with length % 4 == 0 and rows whose threshold is above the `-inf` bin are unchanged. The guard only drops lanes that were never real elements.

## Validation

GPU: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (sm_103), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.14.0+cu130. `_C_stable_libtorch` rebuilt from this branch; main measured with the precompiled wheel for 3e96f9cf6.

New test, `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py::test_persistent_topk_masked_row_tail`. It covers k in {512, 1024, 2048}, length = k + {1, 2, 3, 4}, 0 or 100 finite scores, and in-row fill of `-inf` or `-1e30`:

```text
pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py -k masked_row_tail
main:     36 failed, 12 passed   (every length % 4 != 0 case fails; % 4 == 0 passes)
this PR:  48 passed
```

Sample failure on main: `AssertionError: row 0: indices outside [0, 513): [513, 514, 515]`.

Op-level repro (1 row, k = 512, stride 516, every in-row score `-inf`, padding 0.0):

```text
            main                      this PR
len=513:    [513, 514, 515]           []
len=514:    [514, 515]                []
len=515:    [515]                     []
len=516:    []                        []
```

compute-sanitizer memcheck, one row of length 513 that is also the tensor width, `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`:

```text
main:     3 x "Invalid __global__ read of size 4 bytes" in histogram_2048_topk<512>, kernel aborts
this PR:  ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors
```

Full file with this PR: `pytest tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py` gives 294 passed, 44 skipped (platform-gated cases).

No end-to-end serving repro: no shipped model reaches this path (see Details). CI runs this test file on Blackwell (`.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml`).

## Details

Root cause. The last float4 load of a row (`load_float4_predicated`) fills the lanes past `seq_len` with `-inf`. They are binned like real elements. The collection loop gates candidates only on `vec_valid = i < n_vec`. When fewer than k in-row scores are above the `-inf` bin, the threshold is that bin, so the tail lanes become "equal" candidates. Refinement then reads `logits[idx]` for them and can output them.

Fix. Add `in_range = vec_valid && elem_idx < seq_len` and use it for `is_above` and `is_equal`. Tail lanes still count in the histogram, but that does not move the threshold. They only add to the `-inf` bin, the lowest non-NaN bin, so the counts above it are unchanged. And since `seq_len > k`, the in-row elements alone already reach k at the `-inf` bin.

Reachability, and why there is no end-to-end repro. The kernel path needs a decode row with k < length <= 8192, at most 32 rows, and the persistent backend. The persistent backend is picked by `--sparse-indexer-topk-backend persistent`, by `auto` on SM12x and pre-SM90 GPUs, or by `auto` when the logits row stride is not divisible by 4. The bug also needs fewer than k in-row scores above the fp16 `-inf` bin. I checked every in-tree caller:

- DeepSeek V3.2 / GLM-5 style DSA decode (`sparse_attn_indexer`): in-row scores come from `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` and are finite. Prefill uses `top_k_per_row_prefill`, not this kernel.
- Qwen4-exp QSA: scores are sums of ReLU terms, so they are finite and >= 0.
- Step5 rejects the persistent backend.
- DeepSeek V4.1 `apply_candidate_mask` does write `-inf` inside decode rows. But the shipped DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash config keeps 2048 candidate blocks of 8 tokens (16384 positions) on full-length (`compress_ratio` 1) layers. Every row on this path (<= 8192) is therefore fully covered.

So no shipped model reaches the bug with default or near-default flags. Reaching it needs a config with `candidate_topk_blocks * candidate_block_size < index_topk`, or more than `length - k` scores at or below about -65504. The layer-level script in the issue shows the V4.1 composition (`apply_candidate_mask` then `SparseIndexerTopk("persistent")`) with such a candidate set. If the bug were hit, `triton_convert_req_index_to_global_index` only drops `tok < 0`, so the result would be wrong KV slots with no error.

`cooperative_topk`, `histogram_256_topk` and the radix path are not affected. I checked lengths 8193 to 70001 with all-`-inf` rows on main and saw no bad indices.

Performance: one extra compare per element in the collection loop. No measurable change expected; not benchmarked.

title: [Perf] Prefer DeepSelect over persistent_topk for large indexer top-k batches on SM100/SM103
body:
## Description

The sparse indexer decode top-k auto chain is `cooperative -> persistent -> per_row`. `cooperative_topk` applies only within `AUTO_COOPERATIVE_MAX_ROWS`, so anything larger goes to `persistent_topk`. For GLM-5.3-Flash with MTP k=7 at 32 seqs that is every verify batch: 256 rows, all on `persistent_topk`, which bins logits into a coarse histogram and can silently drop true top-k candidates when a trained indexer clusters its scores in one bin (#51782). The vendored DeepSelect extension handles exactly these shapes on the SM100/SM103 family and measured 191 us vs 616 us at 256 rows / 1M KV when it landed (#56464), but it stayed opt-in only.

This adds a `deep_select` branch in `_resolve_auto` between cooperative and persistent. The existing support checks (`_has_deep_select`, `_HAS_DEEP_SELECT_C`, `is_deep_select_supported`) stay, so other devices and unsupported strides/dtypes fall through to `persistent_topk` unchanged.

Measured on GLM-5.3-Flash (NVFP4), 8x B300 (SM103), TP8, FP8 KV cache, MTP k=7, 1M context, `vllm bench serve`, random dataset, seed 42, medians of 3 warm runs:

| workload (1024-in / 1024-out) | TPOT mean | TPOT p99 | TTFT median |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 concurrent | 5.40 -> 5.05 ms (-6.5%) | 8.26 -> 7.05 ms (-14.6%) | 288 -> 341 ms |
| 32 concurrent | 7.85 -> 6.89 ms (-12.2%) | 12.24 -> 12.84 ms | 1113 -> 1073 ms |
| 128K prompt, 64 out | 8.24 -> 6.82 ms (-17.2%) | 8.24 -> 6.82 ms | 502 -> 477 ms |

These are medians of 3 warm passes within one boot per arm; across reboots of the unpatched build, c8 and c32 TPOT varied by roughly 25% and 12% on this setup, so the smaller deltas are directional and the workload-level trend is the signal. Measured on GLM-5.3-Flash only; the auto choice also covers the DSA indexer path on this device family, which I have not benchmarked here.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Keep activations MXFP8 between DeepGEMM kernels
body:
## Purpose

DeepGEMM's DeepSeek-V4.1 kernels can hand FP8 activations to each other, but vLLM re-quantized their BF16 outputs before every dense projection: 127 standalone MXFP8 quantize launches per decode step at C1 (TP4), plus the quantize half of the Mega-MoE input staging. This PR wires the FP8 outputs DeepGEMM already provides to the consumers, and runs those consumers on DeepGEMM.

One decoder layer, decode step. `[q]` = standalone MXFP8 quantize launch, `sf` = the UE8M0 group scales.

**Before** — every DeepGEMM kernel returns BF16, and a FlashInfer quantize kernel re-creates MXFP8 before each consumer:

```
attention sublayer
  mega_mhc (post+pre+RMSNorm) ──bf16──┬──▶ compressor score / indexer weights GEMMs (bf16, unchanged)
                                      └──▶ [q] ──mxfp8+sf──▶ FlashInfer GEMM  fused_wqa_wkv
  attention ──▶ fp8_einsum wo_a ──bf16──▶ [q] ──mxfp8+sf──▶ FlashInfer GEMM  wo_b ──▶ reduce-scatter

FFN sublayer
  mega_mhc (post+pre+RMSNorm) ──bf16──┬──▶ router gate + top-k (bf16, unchanged)
                                      └──▶ prepare_megamoe = [q] into symm buffer + pack top-k ──▶ fp8_fp4_mega_moe
```

**After** — the producers emit MXFP8 with packed scales directly, the consumers run on DeepGEMM `fp8_gemm_nt`:

```
attention sublayer
  mega_mhc ──bf16──────────────────────▶ compressor score / indexer weights GEMMs (unchanged)
           ──mxfp8+sf (y_fp8, y_gemm_sf)─▶ DeepGEMM GEMM  fused_wqa_wkv        (not under SP: input is all-gathered in bf16)
  attention ──▶ fp8_einsum wo_a ──mxfp8+sf ((z, sf) output)──▶ DeepGEMM GEMM  wo_b ──▶ reduce-scatter

FFN sublayer
  mega_mhc ──bf16─────────────────────────────────────▶ router gate + top-k (unchanged)
           ──mxfp8+sf written straight into the symm buffer (y_fp8, y_routed_sf, y_shared_sf)
                                                       ──▶ prepare_megamoe = pack top-k only ──▶ fp8_fp4_mega_moe
```

| per layer | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| standalone quantize launches | 3 (+ the quantize half of `prepare_megamoe`) | 1 under SP (`fused_wqa_wkv`), 0 otherwise |
| dense GEMM kernel | FlashInfer CuTe-DSL ×2 | DeepGEMM `fp8_gemm_nt` (1,1,32) ×2 |
| bytes between mHC / einsum and their consumers | bf16 out + fp8 in | fp8 out only |

Pieces:
- `DeepGemmMxfp8LinearKernel` (2D `fp8_gemm_nt`, recipe (1,1,32)); its activations carry a new `QuantKey` `kMxfp8DynamicDeepGemm` (int32 packed UE8M0 scales) so a FlashInfer-layout producer can never be routed to a DeepGEMM consumer or vice versa. The model marks `wo_b` / `fused_wqa_wkv` with `deep_gemm_activations`, and ModelOpt's post-load selects the kernel for them the same way it does for `is_bmm` layers.
- `mega_mhc` wrapper: optional `y_fp8`/`y_gemm_sf` and `y_fp8`/`y_routed_sf`/`y_shared_sf` outputs (DeepGEMM already implements them), reported as a typed `MegaMhcFp8Outputs`; the MoE leg is passed explicitly (`DeepseekV4MoE.forward(staged=...)` → `experts.forward_staged`) and `stage_megamoe_routing` repacks only the top-k.
- `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj(fp8_z=True)`: `fp8_einsum` emits `(z, sf)`; also in the mega-attention backend's `_o_proj`.
- Under sequence parallel the attention input is all-gathered in BF16 after the norm, so `fused_wqa_wkv` stays on FlashInfer there (FP8 all-gather is follow-up work).
- The new `fp8_gemm_nt` variants are pre-compiled by the existing DeepGEMM startup warmup (layers found through the `deep_gemm_warmup_provider` protocol).
- Binds wherever SM100 + DeepGEMM are available (checked at construction; other platforms keep their kernels with a logged reason). No new flag.

Duplicate check: searched open PRs for `mega_mhc y_fp8`, `y_gemm_sf`, `fp8_einsum`, `DeepGemmMxfp8LinearKernel`, `prepare_megamoe_inputs`, `wo_b quantize`, and by touched file. #57679 (restores the `wq_b` query-quant fusion) is complementary and untouched here; #56751 (skinny GEMM, M ≤ 4) quantizes in-kernel for the same projections at tiny M, a separate mechanism; #55505 (input-scale contract) does not conflict.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -v -s tests/kernels/test_dsv41_deepgemm_fp8_chain.py   # SM100
```
```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 64
```
Baseline: the same command on main. `vllm bench serve` random 4096/256, ignore-eos, one server at a time; GSM8K via lm-eval 0.4.12 (5-shot chat, thinking off, greedy, 1319 questions).

## Test Result

4×B200, TP4 + EP4, MegaMoE + SP, FlashInfer sparse MLA, fp8 KV.

- Unit tests: 21 passed (DeepGEMM kernel vs FlashInfer CuTe-DSL at M ∈ {1,4,7,64,300}; pre-quantized input bit-identical to in-kernel quant; `mega_mhc` FP8 outputs bit-exact MXFP8 of its BF16 output, MoE layout bit-identical to `prepare_megamoe_inputs`; einsum FP8 output vs quantized BF16 output; routing-only staging).
- Greedy outputs identical on 8/8 prompts × 64 tokens.
- C1 decode step (torch profiler, 61 steps): GPU busy 7.64 → 6.85 ms (−10 %), quantize launches 130 → 90.

| lane | baseline | PR | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| C1 ×3 TPOT | 6.58 / 6.58 / 6.58 ms | 6.50 / 6.50 / 6.50 ms | −1.2 % |
| C4 ×2 tok/s (TPOT) | 517 / 520 (6.97 / 6.94 ms) | 531 / 530 (6.83 / 6.86 ms) | +2.4 % (−1.6 %) |
| C4 ×2 TTFT | 201 / 199 ms | 184 / 183 ms | −8 % |
| C16 ×3 tok/s (TPOT) | 1347 / 1346 / 1340 (9.92 / 9.88 / 10.03 ms) | 1365 / 1357 / 1368 (9.85 / 9.86 / 9.73 ms) | +1.5 % (−1.3 %) |
| C64 ×1 tok/s (TTFT) | 1848 (2360 ms) | 1880 (2124 ms) | +1.7 % (−10 %) |
| GSM8K flexible / strict | 0.9621–0.9659 / 0.7817–0.7832 (3 baselines) | 0.9644 / 0.7877 | unchanged |

After the plumbing refactor (kernel selection through ModelOpt post-load, typed mHC outputs, explicit staged MoE input): 21 unit tests pass, C1 TPOT 6.50 / 6.50 / 6.50 ms, GSM8K 0.9636 / 0.7915, greedy outputs coherent on 12 prompts.

At C1 the host loop (~6.5 ms/step) bounds TPOT, so most of the GPU saving shows from C4 up. The FP8-output `mega_mhc` variants JIT-compile on first use per prefill shape, like the BF16 variants today (cache persists under `DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR`).

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Share the FlashMLA decode plan across KV cache groups
body:
## Purpose

`DeepseekSparseSWAMetadataBuilder.build()` creates one empty `FlashMLASchedMeta` per DeepSeek-V4 layer type. The first `flash_mla_with_kvcache` call of each type runs FlashMLA's tile-scheduler planner, and the later layers of that type reuse the plan (the comment calls it "shared across all ~60 layers of that type within a decode step").

However, the builder runs once per KV cache group. With the packed KV cache layout, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's sliding-window caches are spread over 8 groups, and each group builds its own holders. So the planner runs once per (group, layer type). A torch-profiler trace of one TP8 decode step shows 18 planner launches in the target model (before layers 0-9 and 20-27) and 3 in the DSpark drafter (one per draft layer), where 4 are enough.

`get_mla_metadata_kernel` is a single 32-thread block with a serial loop over the SM partitions, and every launch sits in front of its layer's attention. On H20 it takes 16.6 µs per launch at 1 request and about 41 µs at 64 requests.

A plan depends on the batch shape and on the values of the decode `topk_length` / `extra_topk_length`. FlashMLA's interface allows reuse only while those values stay the same, but it asserts only shapes and config. Across the KV cache groups of one metadata build pass the values do match:
- The SWA lengths come from the same query and sequence lengths, window, valid-token mask and `replay_start`. Each group builds the mask from its own slot mapping, but every sliding-window group writes each scheduled token, so the masks agree; `replay_start` is one tensor passed to every builder.
- The top-k lengths count the valid entries each index layer writes. Every decode top-k path fills the entries past a row end derived from `seq_lens` and `next_n` alone with -1 (for example `rowEnd` in `csrc/libtorch_stable/sampler.cu`), under the same valid-token mask. So each index layer of a compress ratio yields `min(rowEnd, topk)`.

That second point is also why a group's same-type layers can already share one plan today, though they take their top-k from different index layers.

This PR lets the groups share the holders:
- MRV2's `build_attn_metadata` passes one dict to every group's `CommonAttentionMetadata`, next to the existing `_token_to_req_indices_cache`.
- The sliding-window builder takes its plan holders from that dict, keyed by its block size, causality and index width.

What stays as before:
- Callers that do not pass the dict (the V1 runner, the draft metadata refresh of the autoregressive speculator) keep one plan per group.
- DBO micro-batches and the DSpark drafter build in separate passes, so they never share a plan.
- SM100 does not take this path: it defaults to FlashMLA mega attention, which does not use these plan holders.

Planner launches per decode step drop from 21 to 4.

**Duplicate check.** `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search` for `tile_sched`, `FlashMLASchedMeta`, `get_mla_metadata`, `tile scheduler` and `planner flashmla` shows no PR that shares the plan across KV cache groups.

Related: #58762 (RFC #58638) reuses Mamba/GDN metadata across KV cache groups in the same `build_attn_metadata` loop. This PR does the same for DeepSeek-V4's FlashMLA plans, which are built per group however many groups there are.

## Test Plan

**Setup**
- Hardware: 8× H20 (SM90, 96 GB, NVLink).
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, HF revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Prototype Engram to delayed mHC input fusion
body:
## Overview

Prototype an opt-in fusion of the DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram gate/residual update with the following delayed mHC input collapse and RMSNorm. This is a **Draft for implementation review; GPU correctness, performance and model validation are pending**.

Inspired by the DP fusion in [SGLang #43065](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43065). Related vLLM tracking: [#57448](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57448).

## Claims

- Add a producer path that returns both the updated BF16 residual and the normalized input formed with the incoming pre-mix.
- Reuse the existing mHC `stats` specialization to generate the next coefficients without repeating the input collapse and normalization.
- Keep the prototype **off by default**. `VLLM_USE_ENGRAM_MHC_FUSION=1` selects it only on CUDA Blackwell with TP1, no sequence parallelism, and no active mHC overlap stream.

No speedup or GPU numerical-equivalence claim is made yet.

## Validation

Completed local checks: Ruff, six-file Python AST parsing, `git diff --check`, and independent source review. The extracted WKV preparation statements match the original preparation AST. The full pre-commit invocation passed its applicable hooks except for a macOS mypy error on the unchanged `mmap.MADV_HUGEPAGE` access. The original main source reproduces the same error under `--platform darwin`; the hook's mypy 1.20.2 passes all four changed source files and both test files with `--platform linux --python-version 3.11`. No source change or error suppression was used for that platform check.

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/envs.py \
  vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py \
  tests/kernels/test_engram.py \
  tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py
mypy --platform linux --python-version 3.11 \
  vllm/envs.py vllm/model_executor/kernels/mhc/tilelang.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py
mypy --platform linux --python-version 3.11 --follow-imports skip \
  tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py
```

One parametrized regression was added to the existing Engram suite, covering empty/single/odd token counts, shorter KV input, identity and carried pre-mixes, gate masks including a masked NaN, both BF16 rounding boundaries, and CUDA graph replay after changing and restoring inputs. Two existing fake-decoder setups initialize the new flag to false. **These GPU tests have not been run yet**:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py \
  -k 'fused_engram_post_wkv or engram_mhc_preserves_delayed_input' -q
python -m pytest tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k 'deepseek_v41_decoder_mixes or deepseek_v41_capture_previous_aux' -q
```

Before requesting review readiness: compile and validate on B300; compare the complete gate + coefficient projection + stats/input sequence using interleaved graph microbenchmarks; then measure cold DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash prefill on two B300s with TP1/DP2/EP2, 16K chunk per rank, APC/EPLB off, output length 1, three independent AB/BA/AB rounds at 64K/c8 and 32K/c4, 32K/c8, 64K/c4 regression checks. Model output checks are also pending. A kernel improvement alone will not be reported as model throughput improvement.

## Details

The Engram boundary currently materializes the updated residual before delayed mHC reads it again for the input collapse. The new token program computes the HC gates, writes the same BF16 residual, and accumulates the incoming pre-mix collapse while those values are available. It rounds the collapse to BF16 before RMSNorm. The separate coefficient projection still consumes the complete updated residual and produces all next pre/post/residual coefficients using the existing math.

The full residual store, WKV computation, previous-layer auxiliary observation point, mask arithmetic, and both BF16 rounding boundaries are retained. This does not fuse communication or remove coefficient work. Triton and TileLang can use different normalization reduction trees; the regression reuses the existing delayed-mHC normalization tolerance rather than claiming bitwise normalized outputs.

One token program serializes the HC gates, which may cost more than the saved read/normalization work. Register pressure and whole-model benefit need measurement. The default-off switch keeps this unvalidated prototype explicit while those results are collected.

Duplicate checks covered current open `engram mhc` PRs, the #57448 tracker and linked work, and complete public Engram/mHC and Engram/fused searches. No matching vLLM gate-to-delayed-input fusion was found. [#56633](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56633) retains a separate Engram boundary; [#60153](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60153) excludes it. This is separate from packed Engram lookup [#59923](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59923) and WKV sharding [#58678](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58678). SGLang #43065 is prior art for the fusion, not a claim of original invention here.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Share Engram host tables as host-NUMA cuMem across DP ranks
body:
## Overview

With `dp_shared_memory`, node-local DP ranks share one registered `/dev/shm` mapping for the Engram host tables (2 layers x 94.4 GiB on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash). Lookups are random row reads and on GB200 they are bound by GPU TLB misses: the registered mapping uses 64K pages.

This PR allocates the shared table as host-NUMA cuMem instead, which the GPU maps with 2M pages. Rank 0 creates it and broadcasts a FABRIC handle; the other node-local DP ranks import and map it. Where FABRIC handles are unavailable (probed once: create + export), the existing `/dev/shm` path is used and logged. Rank 0 decides the backing and broadcasts it so every rank runs the same collectives. A mapping failure on any rank raises on all ranks.

- New NVIDIA-only `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/ops/engram_host_table.py` (~125 lines of code).
- `common/engram.py`: +42/-7, `DPSharedEngramStorage` keeps its interface; startup log says `via cuMem` or `via /dev/shm`.
- No new config option.

Not a duplicate: open Engram PRs cover pinned sizing (#59849), SP/PCP sharing (#57195, #61553), Mooncake and disk offload (#57023, #62238); none changes the shared host table backing.

## Performance

GB200, DEP4, `--numa-bind`-equivalent binding (`numactl` per rank), dummy weights, uniformly random tokens. Same node, back-to-back A/B.

| 16 | 69 us | 49 us |
| 128 | 184 us | 90 us |
| 1024 | 1.21 ms | 0.47 ms |
| 4096 | 3.78 ms | 1.21 ms |
| 32768 | 9.92 ms | 4.36 ms |

| prefill 4 x 8192 | 347.18 ms | 333.65 ms | -3.9% |

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Share MegaAttn int32 positions across layers
body:
## Overview

MegaAttn converts the same RoPE positions from int64 to int32 in every layer. In a full CUDA graph those casts are separate GPU kernels: 40 per target forward on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Share the converted tensor within the forward context so the graph records one cast.

## Claims

- Removes 39 redundant cast kernels per 40-layer target forward.
- Target GPU time drops from 17.903 to 17.834 ms (0.39%) in the DEP8 decode measurement below.

## Validation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 8 x GB300 across two nodes, DP8 x TP1 + EP, 64 requests/rank, 131,072 input tokens, 2,048 output tokens, attention top-k 1024, DSpark with 5 draft tokens (384 target tokens/rank). FlashMLA built with CUDA 13.4, MegaMoE, Engram on GPU, full decode CUDA graphs. Both runs restore and freeze the same EPLB mapping.

| Target forward | Before | Shared positions |
|---|---:|---:|
| GPU time, median (ms) | 17.903 | 17.834 |
| GPU time, p10 / p90 (ms) | 17.847 / 17.996 | 17.793 / 17.941 |
| Full-batch samples | 366 | 342 |
| Kernels in the captured forward | 766 | 727 |

One run per version on a development tree, using real weights and synthetic KV through `DecodeBenchConnector`. Times are CUDA events around the target graph, without the profiler, taking the slowest of eight ranks for each step and discarding the first ten full-batch steps. Kernel counts come from a separate CUDA-only trace. This measures GPU target time, not request latency or serving throughput.

The measurements used the equivalent helper implementation; the final diff inlines it. The final `forward_mqa` was checked locally on GB300 with a copy consumer: 40 uses share one converted buffer during full capture, offset views stay distinct, replays see updated positions, independent captures do not reuse another graph's cast, and separate piecewise graphs sharing a context remain correct. NONE, FULL and PIECEWISE cases pass. These local checks are not added to the PR.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_dsv41_mega_attn_layouts.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flash_mla_mega_attn.py
```

Existing layout suite on the development tree: 7 passed. Pre-commit, including Ruff, formatting and mypy: passed. No accuracy evaluation was run; the integer conversion is unchanged. The capture checks above were run outside CI.

## Details

The cache is keyed by the input tensor and scoped to `ForwardContext`. The cast still executes on every graph replay. Eager execution and PIECEWISE capture keep their per-call conversion, since separate piecewise graphs must own their buffers. Check actual stream capture as well as runtime mode: MRV2's full capture can run with mode NONE.

Not a duplicate: searched open PRs for `mega attention positions`, `positions int32`, `mega_attn_positions_int32`, and `MegaAttention reuse`. #60613 fixes a prefill index sentinel; #60543 autotunes the indexer GEMM. Neither shares the RoPE position conversion. No linked issue.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Enable DeepGEMM sparse MQA logits on the FP8 indexer cache

## Purpose

`attention_config.indexer_sparse_logits` (#56254) lets DeepSeek-V4.1's candidate-consuming indexer layers score only the candidate blocks with DeepGEMM's sparse MQA-logits kernels instead of dense logits over the whole context. Today it requires the MXFP4 indexer cache (`indexer_kv_dtype="mxfp4"`), so with the default FP8 cache the flag fails at startup:

```
ValueError: attention_config.indexer_sparse_logits requires the MXFP4 indexer cache
```

The restriction dates from before #61149: the FP8 cache then stored one fp32 scale per token, while the sparse kernels take UE8M0-packed (granularity-32) scales. Since #61149, the SM100 FP8 indexer cache stores each token's power-of-two scale as four equal UE8M0 bytes, which is exactly the MXFP8 layout DeepGEMM expects, and DeepGEMM's sparse kernels already have an FP8 (`float_e4m3_t`, `SM100_MMA_MXF8F6F4_SS`) variant for both the contiguous (prefill) and paged (decode) paths. Its paged accessor reads the same page layout as vLLM's FP8 cache (`PAGE_KV x 128` value bytes, then `PAGE_KV` uint32 scales).

This PR wires the FP8 cache into the existing sparse path, so the decode speedup no longer requires trading the K cache down to 4 bits.

## Results

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4, 4x B300, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching`, greedy decoding. Decode and prefill throughput from a linear fit of wall time against output length (256 / 1024 / 2048 output tokens), each point run twice

| batch x context | decode tok/s MAIN | decode tok/s PR | decode speedup | prefill tok/s MAIN | prefill tok/s PR | prefill speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 x 8K | 6,459 | 6,584 | 1.02x | 124,569 | 126,088 | 1.01x |
| 32 x 100K | 3,920 | 4,117 | 1.05x | 117,066 | 117,774 | 1.01x |
| 16 x 256K | 2,293 | 2,535 | 1.11x | 103,739 | 104,733 | 1.01x |
| 8 x 512K | 1,301 | 1,399 | 1.08x | 85,609 | 87,355 | 1.02x |
| 4 x 1M | 692 | 745 | 1.08x | 62,604 | 63,967 | 1.02x |

Decode improves at every point, with up to 11% higher decode throughput. Prefill is at parity: decoder SWA bounded replay (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58132) runs the candidate-consuming layers on only each request's last 128 tokens during prefill, so little prefill indexer work is left for the sparse path to remove.

<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR adds an NVIDIA specialized decode for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on GB300, for the small decode batches that agentic serving runs. It supports:
- one GB300 tray at TP4;
- DSpark speculative decoding with 5 draft tokens;
- FULL-graph decode steps of up to 384 rows (64 requests × 6 tokens). Prefill, mixed batches and larger batches fall back to the stock forward.

It is opt-in via `--additional-config '{"decode_backend": "latency_specialized"}'`, the same switch as #61867. With the default (`auto`), the model runs exactly as on upstream `main`. The model changes are all under `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/`; outside it, the PR only adds tests and a CI step.

The integration follows #61867: the model owns a decode executor that takes over FULL-graph decode steps. The stacked follow-up #61869 puts the DSpark draft model on the same executor. Both follow the RFC #59665 fast-track process. Related: #57448 (DeepSeek-V4.1 tracking), #59725 (Cake kernels).

## Claims

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one GB300 tray with DSpark, the same build with the switch on and off:
- Decode step (one speculative step, including the draft): **18.3% faster at batch 1** (5,355 → 4,375 µs), 13.7% at batch 8 and 11.3% at batch 32.
- InferenceX AgentX traces: **P90 interactivity up 16–24%** at every concurrency from 1 to 64, with throughput per GPU up 1–6% and TTFT unchanged.
- GSM8K, GPQA-Diamond, AIME25 and RULER NIAH stay within one point of the switch-off model, and the DSpark acceptance length does not change.

## Validation

### Correctness

The reference is the same build with the switch off. GPQA-Diamond and AIME25 use reasoning effort high and temperature 0.6.

## Details

### Where the time goes

Agentic workloads such as AgentX send long multi-turn conversations (median 350K tokens of context, almost all prefix-cached) and wait for each reply before sending the next turn. Each server therefore decodes only 1 to 64 requests at a time, and users see the time per output token.

At batch 1, stock vLLM's speculative step takes about 5.4 ms: one target forward that verifies six tokens, plus the DSpark draft. There is no single hotspot.

- **GPU.** A step runs about 1,600 kernels, most of them a few microseconds long. One target layer without an indexer is a serial chain of about 105 µs: about 50 µs of attention (quantize, `wq_a`/`wkv`, norm-quant, `wq_b`, KV insert, index build, `q_lens` and counter fixes, FMHA, `wo`, publish, all-reduce) and about 53 µs of MoE (front 14, GEMM1 19, GEMM2 12, finalize and all-reduce 6). The GEMMs see 1 to 48 rows but run kernels tuned for larger batches; the all-reduce + mHC at each of the 80 sublayer boundaries is fused only up to 16 rows; and layers with the sparse-attention indexer add their own chain of small kernels (logits, top-k and index tables).
- **Host.** The host loop is busy about 4.95 ms of the 5.37 ms step, and about 2.2 ms of that builds attention metadata for the target's and the draft's KV-cache groups. A GPU-only speed-up beyond about 0.4 ms would just expose the host.

So the executor removes kernels and launch gaps, uses kernels sized for 1 to 8 rows, moves independent work onto side streams, and takes host work out of the step loop.

### What changed

Each row is one optimization and the saving we measured when it was added, as a batch-1 decode-step ABBA on one tray unless a batch is named. They were measured one at a time on a development branch, so they do not add up exactly to the end-to-end figure. The full list of paths and their gates is in `nvidia/specialized_decode/AGENTS.md`.

| Optimization | Why | Saving when added |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Fused all-reduce + mHC** | | |
| One fused Lamport all-reduce + mHC kernel at every sublayer boundary up to 384 rows (stock: 16). The next layer's mHC coefficients are computed on a side stream up to 48 rows. | Above 16 rows, the stock path runs a separate all-reduce, mHC and copies at each boundary. | −11.4% at batch 8 (48-row cap); −4.5% at batch 32 (384-row cap) |
| The fused kernel also writes the next attention input as MXFP8. | That removes a separate quantize kernel per layer. | −54 µs |
| `wo_b`'s GEMM epilogue stores straight into the fused kernel's mailbox. | That removes a copy kernel; the fused kernel then only collects. | −41 µs |
| The MoE finalize is deferred into the fused kernel at the Engram and final boundaries too, in a residual-only variant. | These boundaries previously ran the finalize and all-reduce separately. | −36 µs |
| The aux hidden-state means for DSpark are computed on the mHC side stream. | They were on the critical path. | −23 µs |
| **GEMMs for 1–8 rows** | | |
| Routed experts: one fused front kernel (routing, MXFP8 quantization, permutation) and two `tcgen05` GEMM kernels, all in CuTe DSL. The top-k reduction is left to the next boundary's fused kernel. | FlashInfer's TRT-LLM-gen MoE path is tuned for larger M and launches more kernels. | −192 µs (GEMMs), −114 µs (front and finalize) |
| `fused_wqa_wkv`, `wq_b` and `wo_b` on FlashInfer's low-latency CuTe DSL MXFP8 GEMM, with tactics pinned per shape. | The stock MXFP8 GEMM is a persistent kernel sized for larger batches. Pinning keeps the fastest measured tactic per shape instead of the autotuner's pick. | −53 µs, then −62 µs from pinning |
| Compressor, indexer-weight and indexer `wk` projections on vLLM's low-batch BF16 split-K GEMM. The index key store reads `wk`'s FP32 output. | At 1–8 rows these skinny GEMMs give cuBLAS few output tiles; split-K spreads the long K over the SMs. | −60 µs |
| LM head on FlashInfer's CuTe DSL BF16 GEMM, and logits gathered with the custom all-gather. | The stock path uses cuBLAS plus an NCCL all-gather. | −15 µs, −27 µs |
| **Sparse-attention indexer and attention** | | |
| Compressed layers that share an index source reuse one sparse-index table. Sparse-MLA decode launches on a KV-counter buffer that is zeroed once. | Each layer rebuilt the same table and zeroed counters before every launch. | −207 µs (1,578 → 1,486 kernels per step) |
| The tables of every KV-cache group are built once per key, on a side stream. | Each group rebuilt its tables serially. | −103 µs |
| Candidate blocks are selected with `cooperative_topk` over the valid columns. | The stock top-k scans the padded width. | −86 µs |
| Indexer query, compressor and index-key work, and candidate expansion with its MQA-logits schedule, run on side streams. Each joins at its first reader. | They are independent of the attention chain until then. | −50 µs, −33 µs |
| Dense indexer rows are sharded over the TP ranks and all-gathered, on pure-decode steps of at least 8 requests. | The indexer is replicated on every rank, and its cost grows with batch and context. | −1.9% at batch 8, −7.6% at batch 32 |
| **Host and launch overhead** | | |
| Attention-metadata builds are recorded into CUDA graphs at capture, one per decode batch shape and KV-cache group, and replayed. | These Python and Triton builds were about 2 ms of the host loop. | −86 µs, then −27 µs |
| Each Engram layer's KV projection chain (table-row lookup, all-gather, MXFP8 quantize, `wkv` GEMM) runs ahead of the layer on the Engram prefetch stream. | It reads only table rows looked up from the token IDs, so it need not wait for the layer's input. Each Engram layer's main-stream span drops from 70 to 6 µs. | −90 µs |
| Decode steps skip the per-request replay-start upload when the device already holds zeros. | Decode steps only ever upload zeros. | −24 µs |

### vLLM integration

As in #61867, the model owns a decode executor (`specialized_decode/runtime/decode.py`). With the switch on, the model returns a model state subclass (`specialized_decode/runtime/model_state.py`) that builds the executor once the weights are loaded, then tunes and compiles its kernels before memory profiling. For each forward, the model asks the executor for a step (`plan()`). Only FULL-graph captures of pure decode steps of up to 384 rows get one. The backbone runs its embedding and Engram hashing as usual, then hands its decoder layers to the step (`run()`). Every other forward runs the stock layers, which the executor does not modify.

| Package (`nvidia/specialized_decode/`) | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `__init__.py` | The opt-in, and `unsupported()`, which lists every requirement the deployment misses |
| `runtime/` | The executor and its per-step gates, the model state, warm-up, attention-metadata CUDA graphs |
| `boundary/` | The mHC between sublayers on the fused all-reduce + mHC kernel, and the publishing `wo_b` GEMM |
| `attention/` | Low-batch MXFP8 and BF16 projections, the row-sharded indexer, candidate overlap, shared sparse-index tables and the sparse-MLA decode |
| `moe/` | The MoE step with a deferred finalize, and the low-batch routed-expert kernels in CuTe DSL |
| `engram/` | The Engram KV projection ahead of the decoder layers |
| `logits/` | The low-batch LM head and the logits gather |

**Scope.** The switch is validated on one deployment:
- GB300 (SM103), MRV2, TP=4, with no PP, DP, EP or CP and no micro-batching;
- DSpark without adaptive verification;
- `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` with an fp8 KV cache and the MXFP4 indexer with sparse logits;
- FULL graphs for decode only;
- no `torch.compile` of the model (the executor runs inside the forward), and no sleep mode (the routed-expert GEMMs and the publishing `wo_b` bind weight addresses);
- DeepGEMM and NVLink multicast;
- no LoRA, KV transfer or batch invariance.

Any other deployment raises at start-up on every TP rank, listing every missing requirement. Eligibility is combined across ranks with a MIN all-reduce, so ranks always agree. We made it an opt-in because the set is validated end to end on this one deployment; within it, each path still dispatches at run time on host state that every rank shares, as #59665 asks. It can become the default on that deployment in a follow-up.

**Rank lockstep.** The paths contain cross-rank collectives, so a rank that diverged would hang rather than fall back. Every per-step gate therefore reads only host state that all TP ranks share: row and request counts, and the graph mode. Nothing is read back from the GPU in steady state. For example, the row-sharded indexer runs only on even row slices, because DeepGEMM's paged MQA logits need 8-byte-aligned indices on every rank.

**With the switch off.** Inside `nvidia/`, the shared files take small seams with the same behavior:
- `model.py`: the backbone hands its decoder layers to the executor's step when it gets one, and the model picks the model state class;
- `model_state.py`: the replay-start upload and the attention-metadata build become methods, which the executor's model state overrides;

- `ops/cute_dsl/all_reduce_mhc.py`: the fused all-reduce + mHC source is parameterized by its row count and variants, and built at 16 rows as before when the switch is off.

**FlashInfer version.** Three paths use FlashInfer internals: the publishing `wo_b` GEMM, the fused kernel's MXFP8 layer input, and the pinned MXFP8 GEMM tactics. title: [Warmup] Cover DSv4 sparse top-k and DFlash input-prep Triton specializations that JIT at first request
body:
## What

Two Triton kernels still JIT-compile at the first real request despite the JIT warmup, found via Triton cache forensics on PD-disaggregated DeepSeek-V4-Flash DSpark serving (per-config `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` timeline + TTIR diff of warmup-time vs serving-time cache entries). Mid-inference compiles are normally just a one-time latency spike, but on a PP rank that also hosts the Mooncake bootstrap HTTP server they hold the GIL long enough to starve the 5s bootstrap query and fail the first PD request (#58543); they would also trip `--jit-monitor-mode=error` (#56693).

**`ComputeGlobalTopkIndicesAndLensKernel`** (DSv4 sparse attention):
- Its warmup keys pinned `topk_indices_stride == topk` (compact rows). C128A prefill actually passes views into the `c128a_max_compressed`-wide persistent buffer (`sparse_mla.py`), so the physical row stride (e.g. 512) differs from the batch-dependent logical width (128/256/512). The warmup now enumerates the padded-stride variants that serving launches.
- `token_to_req_indices` / `is_valid_token` are sliced at arbitrary token offsets at serving time, so their pointer alignment varies per batch. Both are scalar loads, so the divisibility hint buys nothing: they now use `do_not_specialize_on_alignment`, collapsing the alignment variant matrix instead of enumerating it.

**`_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel`** (DFlash/DSpark speculator):
- `BLOCK_SIZE = min(256, next_power_of_2(max_tokens_per_req))` follows the largest per-request span in the batch; the worker warmup's tiny synthetic steps only reach the smallest buckets, and the first large prefill chunk compiles a new variant mid-inference. `DFlashSpeculator.warmup_prepare_inputs()` now launches the kernel once per reachable bucket over the speculator's real buffers, wired into `kernel_warmup()`. The prefill-only producer variant (`context_only=True`, #56957) is covered when that mode is present.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs for triton warmup coverage of these kernels. The DSv4 warmup series ([7/N] #50177, [8/N] #53567, [10/N] #55967), #54345 (prefill metadata JIT), #55918 (logprobs topk widths), and #45601 (sampler top-k/top-p) each cover different kernels; none touch `ComputeGlobalTopkIndicesAndLensKernel` or `_prepare_dflash_inputs_kernel`. This PR follows the pattern established by #55918 (`do_not_specialize_on_alignment` + explicit startup warmup of the reachable specialization set).

## Tests

- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py::test_topk_lens_warmup_uses_physical_c128a_buffer_stride` — warmup keys carry the physical C128A buffer stride (new, CPU).
- `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py::test_dflash_warmup_covers_reachable_block_size_buckets tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py::test_dflash_warmup_covers_prefill_only_buckets` — bucket coverage for aggregated and prefill-only modes (new, CPU).
- All three pass; `pre-commit` (ruff, mypy, test-tethering, etc.) is green.

## Model evaluation

No serving-path numerics change: the patch only precompiles specializations that serving would otherwise compile lazily, and drops two alignment specializations that are unused by codegen (scalar loads). The motivating PD both-PP DSpark deployment (prefill PP2×TP2 + decode PP2×TP2, Mooncake) scores GSM8K strict-match 0.9447 on the same stack (#56957), with the compile stalls present; this PR removes them at the root.

AI assistance was used in preparing this PR (root-cause forensics, implementation, and tests).

The earlier AB/BA campaign completed two pairs and an unpaired third A. The time-budget guard refused the final B; all 175 measurements remain retained. The two complete pairs regressed on the primary metric and both 32K cells:

| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 64K/c8 (primary) | 157,798.946 / 157,693.510 | -0.0668% |

The latter added about 1.9 ms per rank in that trace, insufficient on its own to explain the earlier 69–109 ms primary wall-time regressions. Their complete cause is not established.

Both arms used the same previously tuned 88-entry FlashInfer cache and the same explicit original default for one previously untuned indexer shape. Dispatch receipts were checked; the common control preserved all dummy/model computation and rejected other cache misses/fresh tuning. These controls and the existing [DeepGEMM #451](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/451) correctness fix are not part of this PR. Earlier retuned or failed-startup attempts remain separate and excluded. Historical five-arm archive SHA256: `1dadda8a207ed6e9ad708ae62fb9c15355048d66b34e61a9eec154bd3c9fba85`.

- Use a device-side upper-bound search for request ownership, preserving zero-query requests, nonzero query bases, invalid Top-K slots and bounded-replay SWA indices. Request/token counts remain runtime parameters.
- Choose the token tile using `TOP_K`, already present in the compilation key. The same helper supplies warmup compilation, launch grid and runtime tile size. No sequence-length threshold or single-request special case is added.
- Write the complete aligned output row, including `-1` tails, removing a separate fill. Preserve lengths and invalid-slot positions without compacting them. Model precision, selected attention indices and required computation are unchanged.


The same tile helper is used by warmup and runtime. A matched whole-model comparison is still needed to attribute a stable end-to-end speedup to the final selector.

title: [Kernel][DSv4.1] Bump FlashMLA to the 2026.09.30 release and its interleaved V4.1 KV cache
body:
# Overview

Bump FlashMLA to vllm-project/FlashMLA@5dceadb (vllm-project/FlashMLA#30), which syncs upstream's 2026.09.30 release (deepseek-ai/FlashMLA#229). Upstream changed the DeepSeek-V4.1 KV cache records to an interleaved layout, so this moves vLLM's V4.1 cache writers and readers to it and aligns the packed DSv4.1 block to the new decode kernels.

## Claims

- vLLM builds against FlashMLA 5dceadb. V4.1 records (528 B MXFP8, 288 B NVFP4) written by vLLM now use the interleaved layout, and FlashMLA's V4.1 decode kernels and vLLM's own gathers read back exactly what the writers stored.
- DeepSeek-V4.1 serves end to end on SM100 with both FlashMLA backends; GSM8K is in the table below.
- KV capacity: a packed DSv4.1 block now has to hold whole rows of both V4.1 records. Relaxing the indexer's DeepGEMM alignment to 256 B (possible since #61149) keeps the loss at 9.5% instead of 24.6% on DSv4.1-Flash with MegaAttention.
- V3.2, V4.0, NVFP4 (V3.2 geometry) and SM90 keep FlashMLA's legacy kernels; their layouts and code paths are unchanged.

## Validation

GB200 (SM100), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (DP4 x TP1 + EP), DeepGEMM mega MoE, MXFP4 indexer cache with sparse logits, DSpark (5 tokens), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 8192`. GSM8K: lm-eval, 1319 problems, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, 1024-token cap, concurrency 32.

| | block (B) | KV memory (GiB/GPU) | GPU KV cache (tokens) | GSM8K strict-match |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MegaAttention (`nvfp4_ds_mla`), main | 114,688 | 63.81 | 2,307,478 | |
| MegaAttention (`nvfp4_ds_mla`), this PR | 126,720 | 63.69 | 2,084,294 | 92.87% (±0.71) |
| MegaAttention, this PR with the indexer kept at 512 B | 152,064 | 63.81 | 1,740,323 | |
| `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` (`fp8_ds_mla`), this PR | 194,304 | 59.32 | 2,457,007 | 92.87% (±0.71) |
| `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41`, this PR with the indexer kept at 512 B | 202,752 | 59.78 | 2,372,929 | |

The main and 512 B rows ran on the base before #61149; KV memory per GPU differs slightly between the two bases. At equal KV memory, MegaAttention has 9.5% fewer KV tokens than main (24.6% with the indexer at 512 B), and `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41` has 4.3% more than with the indexer at 512 B. Every bound KV view had `stride(0)` equal to the block, CUDA graph capture passed, and all 1319 requests succeeded.

Unit tests, with the vendored DeepGEMM on `PYTHONPATH` so the `importorskip("deep_gemm")` cases run:

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert.py   # 374 passed, 19 skipped (ROCm-only)
```
