```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py   # 511 passed, 1528 skipped (Hopper-only or other backends)
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_kv_cache_layout.py tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_native_next_n.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_tp_row_shard.py tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py   # 370 passed
```

New and updated tests:
- `test_v41_cache_writers_match_flashmla_decode` (SWA MXFP8, compressed MXFP8, compressed NVFP4): a token written mid-page into a padded block reads back identically through FlashMLA's V4.1 decode and both vLLM gathers.
- `test_sparse_mqa_logits_paged_matches_dense_masked[page_pad=256]`: the paged sparse indexer decode with a page stride that is 256 B- but not 512 B-aligned, as in a packed DSv4.1 block.
- The existing V4.1 record tests now check the interleaved offsets.

DeepGEMM 6ce1c5e's own `test_sparse_mqa_logits` also passes on the vendored build (644/644, including 196 paged cases with 256 B- but not 512 B-aligned page strides).

CI runs FlashMLA's legacy SM90 kernels in the H100 MLA kernel job. It has no SM100 job for the V4.1 records, so that path is validated only by the runs above.

<summary>Commands</summary>

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe","enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"enable_adaptive_verification":true}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":"VLLM_COMPILE","cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[6,12,18,24,30,36,48,60,72,96,120,144,192,240,288,384,480,576,768,1020,1536,2046,3072,4092,6144,8190]}' \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 8190 --numa-bind
# FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41: same command with "backend":"FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41"

lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash,base_url=http://localhost:8123/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=3,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer_backend=None \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --gen_kwargs temperature=0,max_gen_toks=1024
```

</details>

## Details

**Layout.** Upstream's V4.1 records used to put a page's data rows first and all its scale rows after. They are now interleaved, so token `i` sits at `i * 528` (512 fp8 values, then 16 UE8M0 scales) or `i * 288` (256 Bof e2m1 pairs, then 32 e4m3 scales). The writers (`fused_deepseek_v4_qnorm_rope_kv_insert`, `rope_quant_insert`, the MXFP8 quantize-and-insert in `cache_utils.py`) and readers (the Triton MXFP8 / NVFP4 gathers and the CuTeDSL dequant gather) only change their offsets. The V4.0 record (584 B, separate scale region) is untouched.

**Block stride.** The new decode kernels gather tokens with TMA as rows of a 2D view over the whole cache, so they require `k_cache.stride(0) % bytes_per_token == 0`. DSv4.1 packs every layer's page (SWA, compressed, indexer, compressor state) into one physical block, so each view's `stride(0)` is the whole block. `DeepseekV4SWACache` therefore takes `packed_block_stride_alignment`, and V4.1 sets it to `lcm(528, compressed record)`: 528 with `fp8_ds_mla`, 3168 with `nvfp4_ds_mla`. The KV cache planner already rounds the block up to the lcm of every spec's `block_stride_alignment`.

**Indexer alignment.** DeepGEMM's paged sparse MQA logits address pages as `base + page * stride` with 16 B loads; since #61149 (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33) its guard is 256 B instead of 512 B. main still aligned the indexer to 512 B, which with V4.1 records would round the block up to `lcm(512, 528, 288) = 50,688` B (152,064 B, -24.6%). With 256 B it is `lcm(256, 528, 288) = 25,344` B (126,720 B, -9.5%). With V4.1 records the indexer leaves its page alignment out of that lcm, since the SWA spec now carries the record stride; with the V4 record it keeps the 576 B TMA stride in it.

**Compatibility.** The V4.1 KV cache bytes change layout, so V4.1 KV caches transferred or offloaded between builds before and after this PR are not interchangeable. Decode kernel speed is not claimed here; the V4.1 kernels are upstream's.

**Not a duplicate.** I searched open PRs for `bump FlashMLA`, `FlashMLA pin`, `flashmla.cmake`, `interleaved KV FlashMLA` and `FlashMLA 5dceadb`; none bumps the FlashMLA pin or changes the V4.1 record layout.

title: [Kernel][Build] Bump DeepGEMM to the 26/09/30 release and adapt the sparse indexer
body:
## Overview

Bump the vendored DeepGEMM pin to the tip of `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` `dev` (`6ce1c5e`): upstream's 26/09/30 public release (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#30, deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#462) plus vendoring import fixes (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#31, vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32) and a relaxed paged sparse MQA page-stride guard (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33). Adapt vLLM to the breaking MQA-logits API.

## Claims

- vLLM builds, vendors and imports DeepGEMM 2.8.1.
- The DSA sparse indexer (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, HY-V4) keeps working on SM90/SM100/SM120 with the new MQA-logits API.
- On SM100 the FP8 indexer cache stays numerically identical: same FP8 values and the same per-token power-of-two scale, now stored as four packed UE8M0 bytes (a valid MXFP8 encoding) because SM100 MQA kernels only take MX scales.

## Breaking changes in DeepGEMM `1e1842a` → `6ce1c5e`

| Change | vLLM impact | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| `deep_gemm/__init__.py` imports a new `deep_gemm/locality_domain.py` | not vendored → `import vllm.third_party.deep_gemm` fails | install it in `deepgemm.cmake` |
| `_C.py` registered the locality-domain shim as `deep_gemm._C.locality_domain` | relative import fails when vendored as `vllm.third_party.deep_gemm`, and vLLM then silently treats DeepGEMM as unavailable | fixed in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#31 (in the pin); `tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py` now imports the package so CI catches this |
| The C++ MLOPart bridge imported `deep_gemm.utils.mlopart` and the epilogue module was named `deep_gemm.epilogue` | `localize()` (not called by vLLM) would fail when vendored | fixed in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32 (in the pin): `_C.py` passes its `__package__` to the new `init(library_root_path, python_package_name)` |
| `fp8_fp4_paged_sparse_mqa_logits` page-stride guard lowered from 512 to 256 B (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33) | DeepSeek-V4.1's sparse-logits block stride stays 512-aligned, which still satisfies it | none |
| `fp8_mqa_logits`, `fp8_paged_mqa_logits`, `fp8_gemm_nt_skip_head_mid`, `get_bf16_mega_gate_config` removed | unused by vLLM | none |
| `clean_logits` / `logits_dtype` removed from `fp8_fp4_(paged_)mqa_logits`; `max_seqlen_k` now required (> 0) | wrapper signatures | `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`; prefill chunk metadata carries a host `max_seqlen_k` bound (no device sync) |
| `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` returns **compressed** logits `[M, max_seqlen_k]` (row `i` starts at K position `ks[i]`) on every arch | prefill top-k / candidate-block / DCP consumers indexed absolute columns | consumers run on row starts `0`, ends `ke - ks`; output indices are unchanged (already relative to `ks`) |
| SM100 MQA kernels take only MXFP8/MXFP4 with packed UE8M0 scales, **BF16 weights**, return **BF16 logits**; paged is varlen-only | FP8 indexer (fp32 per-token scale, scale folded into fp32 weights) rejected | see below |
| `bf16_mega_gate` default `scoring_func` → `'sqrtsoftplus'` | vLLM always passes it | none |
| FP8×FP4 / BF16 Mega MoE assert DeepGEMM's SM count equals the device's | only DBO + DeepEP-HT lowers it (`ubatch_utils.py`), not combined with Mega MoE today | none (noted) |
| Epilogue classes (`epilogue=` kwarg), locality domains, `shutdown` | additive | none |

### SM100 FP8 indexer

Every CUDA FP8 indexer writer already stores an exact power-of-two scale `2^ceil(log2(amax/448))` per 128-wide token. On SM100 (`mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()`) the writers store that scale's exponent as four equal UE8M0 bytes instead of the fp32, which is an exact MXFP8 encoding of the same values (same cache size, same FP8 bytes):

| Writer | Models |
|---|---|
| C++ `indexer_k_quant_and_cache` (`scale_fmt="mxfp8"`) | DeepSeek-V2-class `Indexer` (V3.2 via that class, DeepSeek MTP), HY-V4, DeepSeek-V3.2 under PCP |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 fused norm/RoPE (`_fused_norm_rope_kernel`) | DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5/5.2 (`GlmMoeDsa`), Dots3Note, V3.2 MTP |
| DeepSeek-V4 compressor (Triton; the CuTeDSL compressor is head-512 MLA only) | DeepSeek-V4 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 `indexer_k_norm_rope_store` | DeepSeek-V4.1 |
| GLM-5.3 kpool prefill compress + decode update | GLM-5.3 |

Readers need no change: `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache` (prefill, all of the above) and the DCP/PCP gathers copy the 4 scale bytes verbatim, and DeepGEMM reads the paged cache directly. The 512-wide MLA caches, MXFP4 caches, and the MiniMax-M3 / Qwen4 indexers are untouched.

FP8 Q keeps folding its per-(token, head) power-of-two scale into `weights`; `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` passes unit MX Q scales (exact, since `relu(s·x) = s·relu(x)` for `s > 0`) and casts weights to BF16. The BF16 logits are upcast to FP32 for the existing FP32-only top-k kernels (`as_fp32_logits`); routing BF16 logits straight to a BF16-capable top-k (DeepSelect / LiteTopK, #59921/#59922) is a follow-up.

SM90 and SM120 keep the FP8 format, FP32 weights and FP32 logits. Consequently the FP8 indexer cache's scale bytes now differ between SM100 and other architectures: moving that KV cache between SM100 and non-SM100 nodes (cross-generation PD disaggregation, shared KV offload) is not supported for these models. Same-architecture setups are unaffected.

## Validation

All on 4x GB200 (SM100), CUDA 13, torch 2.13; baseline = `main` with the old pin `1e1842a`, same build otherwise.

**GLM-5.3-Flash** (FP8, TP4 + EP, MTP=3, `--max-model-len 131072 --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --reasoning-parser glm47`, `reasoning_effort=low`), on the rebased branch vs `main` bfa7e5b7af. MRCR prompts are far longer than the indexer's coverage (2048 pools × 4 = 8K tokens), so they exercise top-k selection; long prefills also engage the TP prefill row sharding from #54951 (confirmed with a temporary log, e.g. 129K-row steps split `[47458, 18791, 42577, 19957]` across ranks):

| | `main` + `1e1842a` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| MRCR, 60 samples of 16K–32K tokens (`tests/evals/mrcr`), match ratio (2 / 4 / 8 needles) | 0.794 (0.823 / 0.798 / 0.760) | 0.810 (0.904 / 0.791 / 0.735) |
| MRCR, 24 samples of 57K–66K tokens, match ratio | 0.578 (4 runs hit max_tokens) | 0.665 |
| GSM8K (1319, 5-shot) | 90.8% | 91.6% |
| Serving, 4 runs of 128 × (4096 in / 512 out) at concurrency 32, output tok/s | 1492 / 1544 / 1491 / 1471 | 1484 / 1476 / 1337 / 1501 |
| Median ITL | 19.85 ms | 19.9 ms |

GLM-5.3 serving throughput tracks the MTP acceptance length, which varies per run (the 1337 tok/s run had 1.31 vs ~1.7–1.8 elsewhere); runs with matching acceptance agree (1476 @ 1.70 vs 1471 @ 1.71).

**DeepSeek-V4-Flash** (before the rebase onto current `main`; baseline 26a488ad93), TP2 + EP, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`, `--max-model-len 8192`; GSM8K via `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (1319 questions, 5-shot, 2 rounds). GSM8K prompts fit inside the indexer's coverage (512 × 4 = 2K tokens), so this checks the SM100 path end to end rather than top-k selection:

| indexer cache | `main` + `1e1842a` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| fp8 | 95.5% / 94.6% | 94.8% / 94.6% |
| mxfp4 | 94.9% | 94.7% |

**Serving** — same server, `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 512 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos`, one warm-up + 3 runs each, sequential on the same GPUs:

| | output tok/s | mean TPOT | median ITL |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` + `1e1842a` | 2968 (2962–2974) | 18.73 ms | 12.80 ms |
| this PR | 2946 (2928–2958) | 18.89 ms | 12.94 ms |

The ~0.8% gap matches the two extra small kernels per indexer layer on SM100 (weights → BF16, row-aware logits → FP32, ~3 µs together). Feeding BF16 straight from the Q producers and into a BF16 top-k removes both.

**Unit tests** (GB200):

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py                      # 7 passed (SM100 MX + varlen paths)
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_*.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_glm5next_indexer_block_sizes.py tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_*.py \
  tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py \
  tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant.py \
  tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py
                                                                               # 558 passed, 35 skipped
pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py                      # 222 passed
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_deepgemm.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py                                 # all passed
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py -k deep_gemm
                                                                               # 100 passed, 169 skipped
python tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py                                           # now also imports the package
```

`tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_fp8_quant_deep_gemm.py` fails on this GB200 with `unspecified launch failure` identically on `main` + `1e1842a` (pre-existing, unrelated). Not run (no hardware): SM90 and SM120; CI's H100 DeepGEMM job covers the SM90 attention tests. CI has no SM100 DeepGEMM job, so the MX path is validated only by the runs above.

**Pin delta `1448881` → `6ce1c5e`**: the end-to-end runs above used `1448881`. The two later commits change no kernel math (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33 only lowers the host and device stride asserts, vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32 only module naming). Re-checked on `6ce1c5e` on GB200 (the GPUs were shared with another job, so no end-to-end rerun):

```

pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py
                                                                               # 42 passed, 7 skipped (need pip deep_gemm)
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py -k "deep_gemm or deepgemm"
                                                                               # 125 passed, 28 skipped
# DeepGEMM's tests/test_attention.py::test_sparse_mqa_logits, paged cases only, on the vendored build:
# 60/60 passed with 64-token pages of 8448 B (MXFP8) / 4352 B (MXFP4), 256- but not 512-aligned
```

## Details

- `tools/build_deepgemm_C.py` now passes `--force` to `setup.py build_ext`. DeepGEMM's `setup.py` lists only `csrc/python_api.cpp`, so after a pin change that touched only headers (`config.hpp` in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32) an incremental build silently kept the old extension and the import failed with `deep_gemm::init() expected at most 1 argument(s)`. CMake already reruns this step on DeepGEMM header changes and `python_api.cpp` is the only translation unit, so forcing adds no work.

title: [Build] Bump DeepGEMM pin to a6bbb80
body:
## Purpose

Bump the `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` fork pin from `ad1f172` to `a6bbb800` (current head of the fork's `dev` branch), picking up three fixes:

- **[DeepGEMM#9](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/9)** — corrects the ported SM120 GEMM and MQA execution paths, and moves the SM120 regression tests into dedicated `tests/test_sm120_*.py` files so the fork's copies of upstream-owned test files stay byte-identical to `dev` (removes a recurring sync-conflict surface on upstream's per-release test rewrites).
- **[DeepGEMM#11](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/11)** — drops the Mega-Gate finite-score device trap. The selected-expert-ID clamp is retained; non-finite scores now propagate instead of aborting on device.
- **[DeepGEMM#13](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/13)** — raises `kNumTimeoutCycles` from 60s to 300s. That is the device-side spin-wait budget shared by *every* wait in `comm/barrier.cuh`: the NVLink cross-rank barrier, the intra-device grid sync, and the mega-MoE combine peer wait. At 60s it could fire on long-running multi-rank workloads that were still making progress, turning a slow peer into a device assert.

Both pin sites are updated: `cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake` and `tools/install_deepgemm.sh`, which each carry a comment requiring them to be kept in sync.

## Not a duplicate

Checked open PRs against `vllm-project/vllm`:

```
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "deepgemm"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "bump DeepGEMM"
gh search prs --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open "install_deepgemm"
```

No open PR bumps the DeepGEMM pin. #56266 (`[DSv4.1] Integrate Mega-Gate from DeepGEMM`, draft) is the only open PR touching `deepgemm.cmake`, and it refactors the `FetchContent_Populate` block — it does not change `_DEEPGEMM_UPSTREAM_TAG`. No conflict beyond a trivial textual one if both land.

## Test Plan

The pin's risk is twofold: that the ref is fetchable as declared, and that DeepGEMM's `_C` still compiles against it. The changed `csrc/apis/{attention,einsum,gemm,sm120_dispatch}.hpp` are compiled into `_C` on every arch, so a `_C` build exercises them even on non-SM120 hardware.

1. Confirm the new ref is the `dev` head and fetches with the two submodules `deepgemm.cmake` declares (`third-party/cutlass`, `third-party/deep_jit`).
2. Build `_C` at the new pin using `tools/build_deepgemm_C.py` — the same script `deepgemm.cmake` drives.
3. `pre-commit run` on the changed files.

## Test Result

```console
$ git ls-remote https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM.git dev
a6bbb8000161c0dc3a85a0300a905f76898a7913        refs/heads/dev
```

title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Keep the Engram all-to-all buffers in one allocator
body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4.1 with host-offloaded, DP-sharded Engram tables (`cpu_offload: true`, `dp_shared_memory: false`, e.g. with `use_thp: true`) hangs in the first forward (memory profiling) when `--enable-cumem-allocator` is set. This receives the Engram all-to-all into a persistent buffer allocated next to its send buffer, so both come from the same allocator.

No open PR covers this (searched open PRs/issues for Engram all-to-all, cumem, `NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER`). #62091 changes only the GPU-table path (`cpu_offload: false`), which has no all-to-all.

## Claims

- Fixes the hang: DSv4.1-Flash DEP2/DEP4 prefill with host DP-sharded Engram + `--enable-cumem-allocator` now starts and serves.
- No numerical change: the same bytes are exchanged, only the receive buffer's allocation changes. Peak memory is unchanged (the per-step `empty_like` of the same size becomes persistent).

## Validation

GB200 (4 GPUs/node), vLLM nightly 49cb2bbf image (CUDA 13.4, NCCL 2.32.3), env `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1 NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1 NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1`. The changed code is identical on main.

Serving: `vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --enable-cumem-allocator --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"embedding_across_dp":true,"use_thp":true}' --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}' ...` (same hang with DEP2).

| run | result |
|---|---|
| main | hangs in `determine_available_memory`; all ranks in `EngramBatch._stage` `all_to_all_single` (py-spy, also with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`), GPUs spin at 100%, NCCL watchdog fires after 600 s |
| main, no `--enable-cumem-allocator` | starts |
| main, `NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER=0` | starts |
| this PR | starts (profiling + CUDA graph capture); 48/48 completions with 8 to 30K-word prompts at concurrency 16 (both the all-to-all and the peer-exchange slots) |

Standalone reproducer, no model (4 GPUs):

<details>
<summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
# torchrun --nproc-per-node 4 repro.py [--same-pool]
import os
import sys

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist

from vllm.device_allocator.cumem import CuMemAllocator

torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
dist.init_process_group("nccl")
shape = (32768 * dist.get_world_size(), 2, 6, 264)
with CuMemAllocator.get_instance().use_memory_pool(tag="weights"):
    sent = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
    pool_recv = torch.zeros(shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
recv = pool_recv if "--same-pool" in sys.argv else torch.zeros_like(sent)
dist.all_to_all_single(recv, sent)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
print(f"rank {dist.get_rank()} ok")
```

</details>

| send | recv | result |
|---|---|---|
| cumem pool | caching allocator | hangs (killed after 120 s) |
| cumem pool | cumem pool (`--same-pool`) | ok |
| cumem pool | caching allocator, `NCCL_LOCAL_REGISTER=0` | ok |

`pre-commit run --files vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py` passes. No test added: reproducing needs 4+ GPUs with NCCL 2.32 and the cumem allocator, which CI does not run for DSv4.1; validation above was done outside CI.

## Details

Root cause: `EngramBatch.__init__` runs during model init, inside the cumem pool when `--enable-cumem-allocator` is set, so `packed_rows` (the all-to-all send buffer) is a cumem allocation. The receive buffer was `torch.empty_like(rows)` in each forward, from the caching allocator. With NCCL local user-buffer registration on (the default), NCCL 2.32 hangs an all-to-all whose buffers mix the two allocators; the reproducer shows this without the model. I did not pin down the NCCL-internal reason (the serving logs show FABRIC IPC registration failures for some buffers, the reproducer hangs without them).

Allocating the receive buffer next to `packed_rows` keeps both in one allocator in either mode, and removes a per-step allocation. `_stage` is an eager break, so the persistent buffer does not affect CUDA graphs.

title: [Model][DSV4.1] Support MXFP4-packed Engram embedding tables
body:
## Overview

Support DeepSeek-V4.1 checkpoints whose Engram embedding table is stored as MXFP4 (E2M1 nibbles packed two per byte, UE8M0 block-32 scales) instead of FP8. FP8 behavior is unchanged.

## Claims

- A checkpoint with `quantization_config["engram_embed_quant"] = "mxfp4"` now loads: the table is allocated as `[rows, dim // 2]` uint8 and decoded in the lookup kernel.
- The packed table halves the host memory: 12.16 GiB per rank vs 23.60 GiB for FP8 (`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, TP=4).
- GSM8K accuracy of the packed checkpoint matches the FP8 baseline (0.967 vs 0.966), including with `dp_shared_memory`.
- An unknown `engram_embed_quant` value raises instead of being ignored.

## Validation

### End to end (GB300)

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, one GB300 node per run, on `vllm 0.31.1rc1.dev360+g44f0ddfd7` (this PR's base). Compiled ops come from the precompiled wheel for that commit, with this PR's Python overlaid. GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, chat endpoint, `--max-tokens 4096`.

| Run | Engram table | Parallelism | GSM8K acc. | Invalid | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FP8 baseline | 23.60 GiB per rank (host-pinned) | TP=4 | 0.966 | 0.004 | 1275 |
| MXFP4-packed | 12.16 GiB per rank (host-pinned) | TP=4 | 0.967 | 0.005 | 1218 |
| MXFP4-packed, `dp_shared_memory` | 48.64 GiB shared across 4 DP replicas | DP=4, TP=1, EP | 0.967 | 0.003 | 1299 |

- One run per row. A 0.001 accuracy gap is within noise (about ±0.5 points standard error). tok/s is not a clean comparison (single runs, different parallel layouts).
- DP-shared packed storage (`DPSharedEngramStorage`) loads and serves correctly.
- The FP8 baseline is `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-nvfp4-experts-blend`. I did not check that its expert quantization matches the packed checkpoint's, so the accuracy comparison is not isolated to the Engram table.
- Not covered: long-context and other benchmarks, DP=4 with FP8.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
# Packed, TP=4
vllm serve <packed-ckpt> --served-model-name m --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 32

# Packed, DP-shared host table
vllm serve <packed-ckpt> --served-model-name m --port 8000 \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --engram-config '{"dp_shared_memory": true}' \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \
  --language-model-only --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 32

# Eval, against each server
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --use-chat-completions \
  --max-tokens 4096 --save-results gsm8k.json
```

The checkpoint needs `quantization_config["engram_embed_quant"] = "mxfp4"`.
</details>

### Unit and kernel tests

Run on 4xGB300 before the test trim in 1800929afd (which removed the `EngramBatch` skip test and the FP8/THP allocation matrix); not yet re-run after it:

- `tests/kernels/test_engram.py`: 127 passed, 2 skipped (THP without offload).
- `tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py`: 27 passed.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format` are clean.

### Lookup microbenchmark

24 columns, us per lookup (FP8 / packed): host-pinned 8192 tokens 356 / 365; GPU-resident 8192 tokens 115 / 156 (the nibble decode); no extra peak GPU memory.

## Details

- `ParallelEngramEmbedding` takes `packed_fp4`; the row size is `dim // 2` bytes when packed. `DPSharedEngramStorage` and the offload memory log count the packed row size.
- `_engram_lookup_kernel` gets a `PACKED_FP4` constexpr (even column in the low nibble); the block scales are unchanged.
- `EngramBatch.create` returns `None` for packed tables, because the staged exchange carries FP8 rows only.
- `Engram._create_embedding` reads the format from the HF config (default `"fp8"`).
- Limitations:
  - GPU-resident lookup is about 36% slower for packed tables (nibble decode). The deployed host-pinned mode is within 1-3%.
  - `can_share_engram_tables` still sizes `/dev/shm` from the FP8 row size, so it over-estimates by about 2x for packed tables. This is conservative, and I left it out to keep the diff small.
- Existing tests that build layers through `__new__` need a `model_config` stub, which this PR adds.
- Not a duplicate: #58782 (DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 hybrid FP8/MXFP4 quant routing, AMD) changes quant config and weights mapping, not the Engram table path. #60938 also edits `engram.py` and `test_engram.py` (Engram to mHC fusion prototype), so it may conflict textually.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Read GPU Engram tables from peers' HBM instead of DP collectives
body:
## Purpose

With `cpu_offload: false`, DeepSeek-V4.1's Engram tables live in HBM, but every lookup still goes through DP collectives: a pynccl `all_gather` of the hash ids and an `all_to_all_single` of the rows on the node-local `edp` group. Decode runs in FULL CUDA graphs, which do not honor `eager_break_during_capture`, so these collectives are captured next to MegaMoE's cross-rank kernels. In DEP decode on GB200, every rank then blocks in `graph.replay()` of the same decode graph at the first real step (seen with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`); host-offloaded tables, with no NCCL in the graph, never hang. I did not pin down the exact NCCL/MegaMoE interaction. This PR removes the collectives instead: GPU tables are row-sharded over the Engram DP group in symmetric memory, and each rank looks up only its own tokens, reading every row from the owning peer's HBM. Lookups need no collective, barrier or graph break.

* **Kernel.** `_engram_lookup_kernel` gains `PEER_ROWS`. With it, `weight` is a per-rank pointer table: a row's owner is `id // PEER_ROWS`, and its scales follow the rows in the same symmetric buffer. Tables are read-only after loading, so reads need no synchronization.
* **When.** `cpu_offload: false`, TP=1 and an Engram DP group (co-located DP replicas). The table sets `dp_size = 1`, as `dp_shared_memory` does, and `DeepseekV4Model` reads that to skip the hash gather and dummy hashes. Host tables keep `dp_shared_memory` / `EngramPeerExchange`, since symmetric memory cannot map another process's host memory.
* **Across nodes.** By default the group stays node-local. With `embedding_across_dp: true` (off by default), GPU tables are split over every DP rank, e.g. 1/32 of the table per GPU at DEP32; all DP ranks must then share one NVLink domain, as on GB200 NVL72. A group with the DP group's ranks reuses `_DP` instead of building a second communicator: a separate 32-rank group cost ~1.1 GiB/GPU and failed `gpu_memory_utilization=0.95`.
* **Not covered.** GPU tables with TP > 1 keep head sharding and its collectives. Peer mode stages BF16 rows per layer rather than `EngramBatch`'s packed MXFP8 rows, so `wkv` quantizes its own input; feeding packed peer rows to `EngramBatch` is a possible follow-up.

## Where it matters

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode-only on GB200, DEP16 / DEP32 (DP x TP1 + EP), 16 requests/rank, MegaMoE, MegaAttention, DSpark (5 tokens, synthetic acceptance 3.51), EPLB, full decode CUDA graphs, `DecodeBenchConnector` replaying an agentic coding trace. Unprofiled steady state (+60 to +240 s), one run each, on a development tree based on `fe4df3df` with #61767; its Engram code is identical to main. Without this PR, `cpu_offload: false` hangs in this setup, so the baseline is the default host offload. GPU tables use `embedding_across_dp: true`.

| -- | --: | --: |
| DEP16 step (ms) | 14.13 | 13.71 |
| DEP16 output (tok/s/GPU) | 3,777 | 3,827 |
| DEP32 step (ms) | 13.15 | 12.90 |
| DEP32 output (tok/s/GPU) | 3,877 | 3,939 |
| Model memory, DEP16 / DEP32 (GiB/GPU) | | 28.9 / 20.3 |

## Microbenchmark

Both Engram layers' lookups for one decode step, 96 tokens/rank, 16 ranks on 4 GB200 nodes, CUDA graph replay with fresh ids, median over ranks.

| Table layout | us/step |
| -- | --: |
| Host UVA (offload) | 233-324 |
| HBM, heads over 4 GPUs + `all_gather` + `all_to_all` (main; hangs in FULL graphs) | 46.7 |
| HBM, rows over 16 GPUs + `all_gather` + `reduce_scatter` | 180.6 |
| HBM, rows over 16 GPUs, peer read (this PR) | 19.8 |

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -q
pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/parallel_state.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/common/engram.py vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py
```

* `test_engram_table_shared_across_dp_replicas` (4 GPUs): the TP1 x DP4 GPU-table case now takes the peer path, asserts that no DP `all_gather` runs, and replays a FULL CUDA graph with fresh ids.
* `test_engram_group_creation_honors_model_and_options`: TP1 x DP4 cases for the node-local group vs `embedding_across_dp`, and `_DP` reuse.

## Test Result

On 4 x GB200: 29 passed. Pre-commit (ruff, format, typos, mypy) passes.

## Accuracy

GSM8K with lm-eval 0.4.13: 1319 problems, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, 1024-token cap, concurrency 32. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MegaAttention, MXFP4 indexer cache with sparse logits, DeepGEMM mega MoE, DSpark (5 tokens), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 8192`.

| | Engram tables | strict match | flexible extract |
| -- | -- | --: | --: |
| this PR, DEP8 over two GB200 nodes | GPU, rows over all 8 DP ranks (peer read) | 92.57% (±0.72) | 92.72% |
| #61371, DEP4 | host offload | 92.87% (±0.71) | |

The first revision of this PR gave 92.87% / 92.95% on the same setup.

title: [Attention] FlashMLA sparse: stage fp8 mixed-batch q/out in the workspace
body:
## Overview

The FlashMLA sparse `fp8_ds_mla` mixed-batch path now writes the head-padded query and the kernel output into the workspace buffers that `FlashMLASparseImpl` already reserves for `max_num_batched_tokens`, so it no longer allocates them on every call. This removes about 4.25 GiB of per-call allocation at 32K tokens per step. That allocation isn't counted by the startup memory profile, so it can cause runtime OOMs.

Related: #59305, #57878. Complements vllm-project/FlashMLA#29, which removes the kernel-internal fp32 split-KV `o_accum` buffer (the other 8 GiB at T=32K). This PR only covers the wrapper side.

## Claims

- On the fp8 mixed-batch path, the padded q (`T x 64 x 576` bf16) and the output (`T x 64 x 512` bf16) are written into the reserved workspace, and the output buffer is passed to the kernel via `out=`. At T=32768 this saves 4.25 GiB per call, measured. The workspace was already reserved, so KV cache capacity does not change.
- Outputs and LSE are bit-identical to the allocating path.
- GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 on 8xH100 (TP8, `max_num_batched_tokens=32768`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.85`) previously hit a runtime OOM in `flash_mla_with_kvcache` during warmup. With this change it serves the same workload without errors, and GSM8K accuracy matches.

## Validation

**Per-call peak allocation.** Single H100. GLM-5.3-Flash TP8 shapes: 8 heads/rank padded to 64, topk 2048, `s_q = T`. Measured through `FlashMLASparseImpl._fp8_flash_mla_kernel`:

| T | before (allocating path) | after (workspace path) | saved | outputs equal |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 0.384 GiB | 0.251 GiB | 0.133 GiB | yes |
| 8192 | 3.068 GiB | 2.006 GiB | 1.063 GiB | yes |
| 16384 | 6.137 GiB | 4.012 GiB | 2.125 GiB | yes |
| 32768 | 12.273 GiB | 8.023 GiB | 4.250 GiB | yes |

The remaining ~8 GiB at T=32768 is the kernel's `o_accum`, which is addressed by vllm-project/FlashMLA#29.

**End-to-end, previously crashing config.** GLM-5.3-Flash FP8, 8xH100, `--tensor-parallel-size 8 --max-num-seqs 256 --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --max-model-len 131072`.
- Before this change: during the warmup with 8K input and concurrency 256, the server failed with `torch.OutOfMemoryError` (tried to allocate 8 GiB with 5.29 GiB free), and 255 of 256 requests failed.
- After this change: warmups at 8K/c256 and 64K/c64 completed with no errors, and there are no OOM lines in the server log. Peak `nvidia-smi` memory.used was 80923 / 81559 MiB. This is tight because `o_accum` is still allocated per call until FlashMLA#29 lands.

`vllm bench serve` results, random dataset, `--ignore-eos`. The comparison is against the existing MNBT=16384 config, which has a larger KV pool (2.66M vs 1.88M tokens), so this is a sanity check rather than an A/B:

| ISL/OSL, concurrency | completed | total tok/s, MNBT 32K + this PR | total tok/s, MNBT 16K baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8192/1024, c64 | 192/192 | 16717 | 16424 |
| 8192/1024, c256 | 768/768 | 20189 | 21522 (KV cache reached 100% at 32K) |
| 65536/1024, c16 | 48/48 | 23357 | 23141 |
| 65536/1024, c64 | 192/192 | 24263 | 25101 |

**Accuracy.** GSM8K, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, using `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` against the server:

| config | accuracy | invalid |
|---|---|---|
| main, MNBT 8192 | 0.919 | 0.000 |
| this PR, MNBT 32768 | 0.914 | 0.000 |

**Tests.**
- New test: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k test_flashmla_fp8_mixed_batch_stages_in_workspace` (H100). 2 passed.
- Existing tests: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k "test_sparse_backend_decode_correctness and FlashMLA and fp8_ds_mla"` (H100). 84 passed, 84 skipped. These include the TP>1 cases that use the mixed-batch path, run with the workspace locked.

## Details

**Root cause.** For `fp8_ds_mla` with fewer than `MIN_HEADS_FOR_BF16_PREFILL` heads per rank (`fp8_use_mixed_batch`), every step makes a single `flash_mla_with_kvcache` call with `s_q = num_tokens`. The wrapper pads q to 64 heads with `new_zeros`, and the kernel allocates `out`, `lse` and `o_accum`, all O(T * 64). The profile run skips attention, so none of this is counted when the KV cache is sized. At large `max_num_batched_tokens`, a full step therefore OOMs after startup.

**Fix.** `__init__` already reserves `(max_tokens, padded_heads, 576)` and `(max_tokens, padded_heads, 512)` bf16 workspace slots for the BF16 prefill path, which is not used in mixed-batch mode. `_fp8_flash_mla_kernel(use_workspace=True)` takes flat views of those slots sized for the FP8 decode padding (the reserved head padding is at least as wide). It zeroes only the padding heads and passes `out=` to the kernel.
- Only the mixed-batch caller turns this on. Pure-decode, HiSparse and separate prefill/decode callers keep the allocating path, because their T is small.
- The returned output aliases the workspace. It is consumed by the `v_up` projection or the DCP merge before any other workspace user runs. The separate prefill/decode path already returns workspace-backed output the same way.
- The q input comes from workspace slot 0, the q-concat buffer, so it doesn't overlap the padded-q slot.
- No new CPU/GPU synchronization: the added checks are host-side shape asserts.
- `lse` is still allocated by the kernel (T x 64 x 4 B = 8 MiB at 32K).

**Limitations.** The kernel-internal `o_accum` (2 x T x 64 x 512 x 4 B = 8 GiB at T=32K on SM90) is still allocated per call and isn't counted by the profile run. That is fixed in vllm-project/FlashMLA#29. This PR removes the wrapper-side share.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Keep FP8 Engram rows packed through TP exchange
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram's CPU/UVA lookup currently expands checkpoint FP8 values and UE8M0 scales into BF16 before the TP head all-gather. This opt-in change stages each selected head as FP8 value bytes followed by its original scale bytes, exchanges one `uint8` payload, then reconstructs the existing BF16 tensor once before `wkv`. At head dimension 256 and 32-value scale blocks, the TP payload is 264 instead of 512 bytes per head row; this is a byte-count reduction, not a measured serving speedup. The original BF16 lookup and exchange remain the fallback for small batches and unsupported configurations.

Enable it with `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"packed_fp8_exchange":true,"packed_fp8_exchange_min_tokens":256}'`. The initial path requires effective Engram-DP size 1, TP>1, non-SP execution, no microbatching/PCP/DCP, and a head dimension divisible by the scale block size. The token threshold is a conservative policy knob pending target-hardware crossover measurements. Persistent packed staging keeps the asynchronous UVA lookup's addresses stable; all TP ranks select the same representation from the batch shape, and the post-exchange dequantization uses the same FP8-to-FP32, UE8M0 exponent and BF16 rounding sequence as the current lookup. `wkv` and the public Engram output contract are unchanged.

This does not duplicate #56929, which begins with a BF16 collective result and fuses head reordering with WKV activation quantization, or #56435, which changes SP redistribution to all-to-all. #56512 supplies the existing CPU/UVA prefetch that this path reuses. If those PRs land, the non-SP transport boundary and end-to-end crossover must be remeasured on the rebased head.

title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Faster Engram host lookups: sorted rows, inline big lookups
body:
## Purpose

Speed up DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram lookups from CPU-offloaded tables. On GB200 they are bound by GPU address translation, not bandwidth: each row misses the TLB on the small pages that back the table.

- **Sorted host lookups.** Large lookups from small-page host tables (pinned or `/dev/shm`) sort their rows by table offset, so neighboring rows share page walks. THP tables skip it, and so do lookups below the sort threshold.
- **Inline big lookups.** From the inline threshold (tokens, max over DP ranks), the lookup runs on the main stream at full width instead of the prefetch stream. Persistent main-stream kernels (MegaMoE, mHC, block-scaled GEMMs) cannot co-reside with lookup CTAs, so a background lookup stalls them anyway, and EP collectives then wait on the slowest rank.

`_engram_lookup_thresholds` picks both thresholds per GPU family: 36864 rows and 4096 tokens on Blackwell (measured on GB200). Other GPUs, including ROCm, keep both paths off and behave as before.

All Engram logic now lives in `common/engram.py`, so NVIDIA and AMD share one implementation and `nvidia/engram.py` is removed.

Also fixed along the way:

- DP replicas share the tables only if `/dev/shm` has enough free space (it used to check the total size). The Engram DP leader decides and broadcasts, so replicas always agree, and peers do not hang if the space query raises.
- The lookup kernel no longer ties the output row index to the id dtype, so int64 ids compile.

## Kernel microbenchmark

Kernel only, single GB200 bound to its NUMA node, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash table sizes (24 heads x 16M rows, 94.4 GiB), uniform random ids, CUPTI median of 3 runs rotating 16 id sets. Grid as in production: 76 CTAs below 4096 tokens, 152 from there. HEAD, new unsorted and new sorted outputs are bitwise identical, and from 64 tokens up the new kernel is never more than 1.5% slower than HEAD below the sort threshold.

DEP2/DEP4 (24 heads per rank, `/dev/shm` table shared across DP replicas):

| tokens/rank | before (us) | after (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 90.1 | 88.1 | 1.02x |
| 512 | 620.5 | 620.6 | 1.00x |
| 1024 | 1236.0 | 1237.0 | 1.00x |
| 2048 | 2463.7 | 2163.7 | 1.14x |
| 4096 | 4621.3 | 3773.7 | 1.22x |
| 8192 | 9243.6 | 5925.9 | 1.56x |
| 16384 | 18476.0 | 8174.7 | 2.26x |
| 32768 | 36963.3 | 9905.1 | 3.73x |

TP2/TP4 (per-rank pinned tables):

| tokens | TP2 before (us) | TP2 after (us) | TP4 before (us) | TP4 after (us) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 1791 | 834 | 440 | 447 |
| 8192 | 3578 | 1846 | 877 | 160 |
| 16384 | 7162 | 3457 | 1745 | 232 |
| 32768 | 14319 | 4291 | 3481 | 396 |

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py tests/distributed/test_engram_dp_shard.py -q
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files <changed files> --hook-stage manual
```

New coverage: the sorted lookup reconstructs the checkpoint under TP padding; a `/dev/shm` that is too small or cannot be queried falls back to sharding, and the leader still broadcasts that decision.

## Test Result

117 passed on 4x GB200. Ruff, format and mypy pass.

## E2E prefill (DEP4)

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 (DP4 x TP1 + EP) on one GB200 node: DeepGEMM mega MoE, FlashMLA mega attention, fp8 KV cache, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, prefix caching off. `vllm bench serve` on random prompts with one output token, so every request is a single prefill. Base (5e887a078b) and this PR ran in the same job on the same node; each point is the median of 3 repeats with unique seeds after a warmup pass. No timed run saw a runtime compile.

| prompt | concurrency | base TTFT p50 (ms) | PR TTFT p50 (ms) | speedup | base tok/s | PR tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4k | 1 | 126 | 128 | 0.99x | 31,961 | 32,060 |

At concurrency 64 every step prefills the 16384-token budget on all four ranks, so those rows share one step shape and differ in context length; their repeat spread is under 4%. At concurrency 1 the spread is up to 11%. Concurrency 4 and 16 are left out: their TTFT depends on arrival order and repeats spread up to 40%.

Where the time goes at concurrency 64 (estimated from the throughput and the microbenchmark, not profiled): a step takes about 280 ms on base and 230 ms with this PR. Sorting saves about 20 ms of it: each step looks up 16384 tokens x 24 heads in each of the two Engram layers, which drops from 18.5 ms to 8.2 ms per layer. The other ~30 ms comes from running those lookups inline, so they no longer stall the persistent MoE, mHC and GEMM kernels on every rank. At concurrency 1 only one rank is busy and the gain (about 24 ms per 16384-token step) is close to the sorting saving alone.

## Accuracy (DEP4, this PR)

GSM8K: 1319 problems, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, 4096-token cap, concurrency 32. Strict match 92.49% (flexible 92.49%), no request errors.

Searched open PRs for Engram storage and lookup work. #58766 (FP8 rows into `wkv`) edits the same lookup kernel, #58310 (reject tables larger than host memory) adds a host memory check, and #57195 shares host tables across SP ranks. title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Exchange packed FP8 Engram rows across DP and feed wkv MXFP8
body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1's Engram tables are already MXFP8 (FP8 rows with one ue8m0 scale per 32 values) and `wkv` is an MXFP8 GEMM, but the lookup dequantizes each row to BF16, DP replicas all-gather those 512-byte rows layer by layer, and `wkv` quantizes them right back. This PR keeps rows packed from the host table to `wkv`.

- **Packed rows, direct MXFP8.** The lookup copies each row's 256 FP8 bytes and 8 scale bytes as they are, and one unpack kernel writes them in FlashInfer's MXFP8 activation layout (F8_128x4 scales). `wkv` takes them as a `QuantizedActivation`, so both the dequant and the requant are gone, and the output is bit-identical.
- **One all-to-all per prefill step.** `EngramBatch` looks up every local Engram layer into one packed buffer and exchanges it with a single all-to-all, which sends each rank only its own tokens (264 instead of 512 bytes per head row, 1/DP of an all-gather), then unpacks all layers in one launch.
- **Peer exchange for decode.** Below 128 tokens per rank, `EngramPeerExchange` replaces the hash all-gather and the per-layer row all-gathers: ranks publish ids in symmetric memory, look up their head shard for every peer's tokens, and read their own tokens back from the peers after a barrier. All layers share one lookup and one unpack launch.

The batched path serves DP-sharded tables (`embedding_across_dp` without DP-shared memory) with TP = 1, `head_dim % 128 == 0`, no LoRA (it wraps `wkv` after construction), and a `wkv` kernel that takes F8_128x4 scales (reusing `can_fuse_query_quant`). The peer exchange also needs SM100, CPU offload, and 2/4/8 fully connected GPUs; without it every slot uses the all-to-all, which on DEP4 HBM tables at 1–127 tokens per rank is 19–58 us faster than the BF16 path. Everything else, including TP, DP-shared tables, single replicas and ROCm, keeps the existing BF16 path unchanged. Communication stays on the current stream and `wkv` still runs in `Engram.forward`.

Also changed along the way:

- `EngramBatch` is an `nn.Module`, so the peer exchange's pointer tables are model buffers that level-2 sleep restores.
- `fused_q_kv_rmsnorm_quant` and the Engram unpack kernel share the F8_128x4 scale offset and size helpers.

## Kernel microbenchmark

The benchmarks, E2E runs and the first accuracy table were measured on d593d7f5df. 3724967bb9 only drops paths that DEP + THP never takes and keeps its `wkv` outputs bitwise identical (see Test Result).

Engram only, two layers (lookup, exchange, and anything needed to reach the MXFP8 `wkv` input), 4 x GB300 in one node. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash table sizes (24 heads x 16M rows, 94.4 GiB per layer) as DP-shared `/dev/shm` tables or private THP shards, uniform random ids rotating 3 sets, 256 MiB L2 flush per sample, full CUDA graph replay, median of 40 samples of the slowest rank, best of 2 rounds. Since this PR's output is already the `wkv` input, the BF16 columns include their activation quantization (17 us for decode, 203 us at 32K tokens).

DEP4:

| tokens/rank | DP-shared (us) | THP + all-gather (us) | this PR (us) | vs THP + all-gather |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 34 | 80 | 36 | 2.22x |
| 8 | 34 | 81 | 38 | 2.13x |
| 32 | 38 | 93 | 40 | 2.33x |
| 64 | 44 | 106 | 43 | 2.47x |
